title: Recent updates seem to have lost the people’s interest
content:
Recently the app has gone through many changes, and here I am. I’d like to say with the update that was pushed to my phone today, it is extremely hard to do much. The media list of people online was hard to find, the separation between servers and messages feels just plain wrong, the removal of numbers. I’ve been using discord since 2018, so maybe I’m being picky. But it seems Discord as a company doesn’t want to listen to its ‘consumer’ anyways. There was negative feedback about the removal of the number system for usernames, the altering links feature which can lead to scamming and hacking, and the lash back about the most recent UI changes.
While I understand that company has to have integrity and be able to reason, I feel that in some stances the Discord company can’t see that certain changes might affect their platform negatively. 
My number one concern is that Discord isn’t listening to its users, you can be firm and have a middle ground. Some of the changes aren’t the end of the world, none of them are. But sometimes the changes can seriously endanger the users, if said users aren’t careful enough.
That being said, the new update of separation of servers and DMs is annoying, the almost inability to find server members and their current online status is so, so infuriating as someone who checks this feature often. Oh, and to put it rather blunt, the new UI is very ugly.
Discord is my number one app, it’s my messaging app, my notes app, I use this app more than I use the general texting app. Please, listen to your users.

title: Wifi vs Data
content:
I’ve had Discord for years, since 2017 and not had a lot of issues with the site other than bots at the time which has gotten a little better ig. I’ve always been able to use Discord with fairly easy use and consistency for the past years, but I’ve also have had wifi for the most part and even being off wifi in the past it has been good before with little issues.
Now, recently, I’ve been coming across multiple issues. I now have no Wifi and have been using Data full time and it has become such a pain to use.
I have Nitro and had it for a year now and for the past 6 months on data and it uses so much Data for one, I’m glad the clear cache is added but doesn’t do much or even really work and still have to uninstall the app when necessary ( apple problem ). The issues I have is messages refusing to load and send at all and can take up to an hour to send one message and have had messages continuously duplicate after each hard reset which is really annoying. Hard resets to the app does not reset the app all the time and takes many and multiple attempts even after waiting a minute or two. Trying to send photos which can and will take longer than an hour just to send or even load and gods forbid I send more than one photo at a time. I’ve had issues with false notifications, and issues with them not going away even after checking and hard restarting the app, multiple times. 
This wouldn’t be as irritating if I wasn’t paying for Nitro, and not the basic at that, and it struggle so hard to do the basic tasks above.
author: SOAPGAVSSUSHWWJHEVEV

title: Don’t fix what ain’t broke— unless it’s to make it better.
content:
I honestly can’t understand what is so WRONG with this new ui. First of all, it is now infinitely easier to see what your friends are playing. I used to have so much trouble seeing whether my friends were online, and it just became so much easier (I also LOVE that the icon of the game they're playing is now so much bigger and more visible). I also like how you separated your DMs and your servers. I used to hate having to scroll up the server list to access my DMs, as I am in a ton of servers, so thank you, discord. I do admit it is a bit weird how now you cannot simply swipe left to see who is online in a server, but you can easily adjust to that. I also love how when you enter a server, the server bar just disappears. It makes things look so much less cluttered and makes it a lot easier to navigate the channels. So really, this new ui is awesome, and I have no idea what people are on about.

I also noticed that people are saying this new update is… buggy? I have no idea what they are on about, as I currently own an iPhone 11 that has been in heavy use by me AND my sister over the last ten years, including multiple cracks on the back due to the multiple times my sister has dropped it, but discord runs perfectly fine. It is most likely a software problem if discord is crashing— just update your software to at least iOS 16 (for apple users, samsung users, sorry you’re on your own ;P)

So overall, I think this was an awesome update, and it really made the mobile discord a whole better experience. If you’re complaining, boohoo, deal with it. :3

author: CyursLight

title: I Love Discord
content: I have never written a review before, for anything. But Discord has become one of the best ways to communicate to my teams that I have built over the past year, I just can’t not write a review about this app. Discord itself has changed my life as cliche as it sounds, but it’s true. Discord has been the stepping stones that led to bigger things, exponentially. First starting using it to keep in touch with a couple friends, which turned into a hangout for a few more friends I met online, to turning into making a server for a clan for clan related stuff, which has now developed into a server for development of a game in production, that can earn me real money doing what I love to do, with those same few people I mentioned earlier. This means of communications is terrific. The app version doesn’t have as many features compared to PC (access to audit logs, not as easy to navigate in, ), but it is pretty much just as good if those things are overlooked, or if mobile is just temporary while you are away from your keyboard. Not only are you able to make your own servers for your own reasons, you are able to customize your server name, picture, voice chat with others with pristine connection, chat channels to keep your chat organized, permissions to who has access to what whether that is channels, roles, even permissions; what you do with your server is up to you. Great for management, a hangout for your friends, .. a development team, how you use discord is literally only limited to your imagination. Without discord, I wouldn’t be in teams I am today, wouldn’t have met some of the coolest people I know

author: Sapphirewarlock

title: Mostly alright, new update is ambiguous
content: This is mainly to address the ambiguous ness of the NSFW IOS ban, since it’s not very clearly outlined. On IOS alone, servers with NSFW content are unable to be viewed now except by mods and owners. Now, the issue with this is that a server doesn’t necessarily need to be NSFW, but simply have a channel as such that can be accessed on it. One of my friends had an NSFW channel in his server, and told me his server was inaccessible because of it. Now, the issue I have with it is that many channels designated as such are not necessarily pornographic channels, but simply oriented for, let’s say, not very politically correct content. And because of that NSFW marking, servers can be shut down even if it isn’t for porno material. Discord should simply reestablish some form of age verification rather than butcher numerous servers because of an unnecessarily ambiguous and broad label. The main complaint is with the Apple store, who does not allow content with such labels on their store, so rather than monitor who can have what, it’s simply a moniker of nobody is allowed, and that punishes those who are allowed to normally access said content unjustly. Sure, that sort of stuff doesn’t have to be your thing, just as it isn’t mine, but people who do take some interest in it shouldn’t be punished by having servers shut down over an ambiguous rule meant to keep kids out of where they shouldn’t be. If Microsoft and apple had any reasonable sense of mind, they wouldn’t ban stuff outright, but limit who sees what

title: Integrated Phone Calls
content:
Discord is an amazing app that lets you do casual conversations without the loud notifications you would usually get from text messages. It does an amazing job at keeping notifications hidden when you want them to be.
But I cannot say the same for calls. Recently, Discord started integrating their calls with actual phone calls. This means that every time I get called on Discord, it goes through to my ringtone. The whole reason I use Discord is to keep my online life separate from my personal life. 
Although there is a setting that allows you to disable this feature, I still get the ringtone. Whenever I get called on Discord, even though the app is closed, I still get a ringtone. I even have all notifications turned off in my settings. The ringtone only lasts about 2 seconds before it realizes that it should not be there, but it gets pretty annoying, since it forces me to stop whatever i’m doing on my phone.
What annoys me the most is that this issue has been fixed before. The previous update had the setting that disabled the integrated phone calls, but it actually did its job, unlike this recent update. I had no calls going through no matter how much I was getting spammed with calls. 
I thought this problem would be gone forever, but it still managed to find its way back. I’ve resorted to having to delete the app just to avoid the ringtone...again. Please fix this issue.

author: David of the Light

title: Absolutely awful new mobile layout
content:
Look, I get that Discord is known to get criticized for every new feature they add before people eventually move on because they realize it wasn't that bad (think back to when when they made the logo symmetrical or when they changed the font). But this is the first time in my three years of using Discord that I've genuinely felt that an update made me want to uninstall the app.  Yesterday I'd have rated the app 5 stars, and today I rate it a 2. The app went from great to clunky, messy, and less usable overnight, which makes me wonder: How? How is this even slightly necessary for improving user experience?

I have many complaints, but my biggest issue is that the swiping doesn't make sense anymore. You can swipe right in DMs, but you can't swipe left to make it go back. The members list is now hidden in the oddest place, the message previews in DMs make the layout look incredibly busy, you can no longer open the list of your friends to see people's statuses and who's online, and you can only use the search function to find things in one channel at a time. It's objectively not a good update, and you'll just end up losing current users like myself.

I don't see why this layout couldn't have remained an optional feature like it used to be. The only thing I maybe enjoy about the change is the color, athough that alone is certainly not enough to make this a good update.

author: Chris or Paul

title: The latest UI is a step backwards
content: The new user interface has a weird flow. It used to be that new direct messages would  appear at the top of your server list, which means you were able to keep your attention on one section of the app. Now direct messages can only be accessed from a separate part of the app that’s accessed from the footer. Now you have to keep your attention not only on the server list to monitor for new activity, but also on the footer, and the footer doesn’t tell you who you’ve received messages from in the same way the old system did (where profile pictures would populate at the top of the server list). Now one must navigate into the direct messages directory in order to see who they’ve received messages from, which takes you out of the familiar Discord interface. You cannot access the server sidebar from here. Before you were able to easily return to the server listing by swiping your direct message to the right, just as you would a server channel. Now swiping away a message reveals the direct messages listing. Now one must take the additional step of tapping on the servers icon in the footer. This may not sound so bad, but it really breaks the seamless flow prior versions of the app had, not only because of the additional inputs, but because of the added spatial and relational complexity. Discord’s UI used to give me the sense that I was in one place, choosing to move things in and out of that place. Now it feels like two places.

title: Each update makes the UI worse
content:

Removal of buttons, removing swipe to see userlist and replacing it with making a thread (which is annoying at best and actively detrimental at worst, especially for those with disabilities), shrinking the size of text, changing the location of server settings, user settings, and user settings WITHIN a server, changing how search functions (you have to click the main server’s search bar to search through the whole server. If you click the search in a channel it exclusively searches that channel. for a while i thought it was now impossible to search an entire server because of how unintuitive this is. The search works worse now, too.).
Most things now require you to click two separate things just to get there, much less actually perform the action you want. Again, this is annoying at best, and actively detrimental at worse. What about people that struggle with fine motor function? What about the visually impaired? Everything is small and inconvenient. It’s way too easy to misclick, or to not know where something is and have to fruitlessly search a bunch of menus just to realize it was somewhere else entirely. The fact Discord keeps changing the location of buttons (and outright removing the dm button from the button of the screen, most recently) certainly doesn’t help. 

I wouldn’t be as upset if there was an option somewhere to use a previous version of the app. Right now I’m stuck using something that apparently tries to be as unusable as possible.

author: chicken nuggies 3826

title: The Absolute Gold Standard of Chat Apps (5/5 Stars)
content:
Discord easily earns a full 5-star rating for completely revolutionizing how we connect and build communities online. Its brilliant server design allows you to organize different topics into dedicated text channels and low-latency voice rooms with absolute ease. Whether I am hopping into a quick screen-share session with friends or managing a massive public group, the platform handles it all flawlessly. The crystal-clear audio and video quality make virtual hangouts feel incredibly seamless and responsive. I also love the endless selection of custom bots, which effortlessly handle everything from playing music to automated moderation. While the dense interface can have a slight learning curve for total beginners, it quickly becomes incredibly intuitive to navigate. It is amazing that the core free experience is so incredibly robust, never forcing you behind an annoying paywall just to talk to your friends. It also runs flawlessly across PC, mobile, and consoles, keeping everyone synced up no matter what device they are using. Ultimately, Discord sets the absolute gold standard for modern communication, making it an essential download that I cannot recommend highly enough.
5 stars

Additionally, Discord integrates with various bots and tools to enhance functionality, making it a robust choice for gaming groups, study communities, or professional teams. Its user-friendly interface and strong focus on community-building make it an excellent choice for diverse communication needs. With these pros, though comes multiple flaws and downsides including latency problems, lack of more free servers, and voice chat system being flawed. With the latency issues, discord can be at times frustrating for its customers. Many times have I lagged while on call with companions. Further more, the calling and voice chat system has experienced multiple flaws throughout its history. Finally, the freedom of customers has been restrained by the devs ever since the beginning of this apps creation.

All of this could’ve been resolved if I had access to someone at discord who knew a lick about user accounts and how to immediately delete them.
author: fuqmyassunderarmor

title: Change for the sake of change.
content:
I’ve been using discord for about 5-6ish years now and it’s been home to a ton of great friendships and stories, or rather, it’s been my home on the internet if you will. I appreciate some of the new features that were added in the latest update, but it also feels like Discord is loosing its identity and is now trying to be like the various other chat platforms available across the AppStore. The iconic grey was changed to a boring blueish color that makes the app have some visual accessibility issues in many places. The intuitive card layout from before is now broken with swipe gestures for the reply feature. I think some of this is just because it’s hard to get used to change, but I really feel like discord is changing things away from what their initial experience was. It used to be home, and now I see no reason to use it over something like telegram or Snapchat, seeing as it’s trying to just be some other chat app. 

Devs at Discord, thank you for the work you’ve put in. I appreciate all the little animations and how hard you’ve probably worked on this, but creating so much change all at once was not the way to do it. A great way to fix this all would be to add more personalization to the app in settings; a toggle to go back to the old grey color for people who have a hard time reading with this new one, a toggle to switch layouts, something like that. I think there’s a fine line between keeping the charm of discord and making it be just a boring old chat app that people don’t want to use, and you’re certainly leaning towards the latter half right now.
author: aleconline

title: Keeps crashing and marking unread messages as read.
content:
I like Discord for what it offers, but the iOS app crashes randomly whenever I try to load a picture, gif, song, or other upload someone else posted, and crashes when I try to post pictures quite frequently. I know that a lot of people upload stuff, so the fact that it crashes as often as it does is a major concern for me. 

Another issue is that the app has decided to randomly mark all messages in random chat channels as read when I open them, even though I’ve still got dozens to read before I reach the end of the string. Or I’ll be reading the messages, and suddenly it marked all messages as read, to include ones that happen while I’m reading, and not even remotely caught up. It happens randomly, so I don’t even know what might be the issue. It might happen to a chat every time I open it, or just once in a while but it’s a bug I want to see gone. Being tagged in a message, and then having that indicator removed randomly is an issue. I don’t always have time to read everything in one sitting, so I want to be assured that I can read it later. It is a major issue when it starts you over at the end of the conversation, and doesn’t save from where you had to leave off. (This is mostly for my admin duties on servers.)

I like that I have the ability to take Discord with me, but if I can’t use it half the time, then it’s like I don’t even have it at all.
author: Gorogokvi

title: Amazing, with several missing opportunities
content:
Discord is a great app, as I myself have been using it since 2018, and it hasn't given me any problems. However, there are some things I wish Discord had that it currently doesn't. Here's some I could think of:
-In servers it would be great if you could mention a role without the person(s) that have that role being notified (maybe a different prefix, like $).
-If, for example, I want to ping people with a certain assortment of roles, such as Moderators that are online at the moment, or Friends that are also Server Boosters. Some way to combine role pings to capture the attention of a more precise bracket of people would be nice.
-I'm in so many servers that it's extremely difficult to navigate through each of them, even with folders. I really think there should be an option to lower the size of server icons, and a new folder functionality, instead of appearing on the same row as others, servers in open folders would travel to the right of other servers, giving space to be able to see every server and navigate with ease
-Slightly similar to the previous point, but there should be an option to make channel tabs smaller. Same reason.

author: crazy cracie

title: Great app but.....
content: I got this app roughly a year ago and it is great, you can connect to any counity you want and even create your own server if you are selling or promoting something. On the other hand, there are things called "server nukes" or some people call it "raids" and basically people will join into your server abd somehow gain permissions to edit channels and completely destroy your server. There are easy ways to protect against this like adding security apps but I won't get into that. My main problem is how many payments are required for basic work, if you want to send a file larger than 10mb then you have to buy discord nitro which isn't cheap, along with that you have to buy discord nitro in order to customize your profile and make it more like your style. Another issue is "server boosting", if you want to unlock special perks for your server, you or other people can boost your server and reach different levels that unlock special features for your server. Not that bad right? Wrong. Each boost runs out after a very short amount of time and boosting costs quite a bit, this means that it would cost like $100 a month to maintain your server perks. Overall it is a good app if you are just looking to find a certain community and talk to people.
author: Emerson B White

title: Stop trying to fix things that aren’t broken. Horrendous mobile update.
content: Your original mobile design was flawless. It was easy to navigate through servers, view who is in each server, and message in dms. I found it extremely impressive how well the desktop app translated into the mobile app. This has been my number one go to messaging app, and I gladly support this company by paying for a subscription because I cherish it so much. Now you all just went ahead and ruined it with the new mobile layout and desktop icon designs. What was the reason? Your users are accustomed to using your app in a certain way and they continue to use it because they like the way it’s formatted. The reason we use this app is because of its seamless navigation, intuitive organization, and uniqueness compared to other messaging apps. You took what makes you special and threw it into a dumpster before setting it on fire. The same goes for your icons on desktop. At first glance I could immediately register what each icon was. Their designs were pleasing to the eye, but the new designs are absolutely atrocious. Not every icon needs to be rounded and simplified. The old ones had character and clean crisp lines. I’m not sure why you guys insist on making these “improvements” instead of listening to what your users actually want and putting your time and money into exploring that. I do hope that this company does thorough user testing before releasing new updates, reverts the mobile update, and takes their users opinions into consideration when moving forward with changes.
author: MaxRuinedMyDay

title: The new UI update ruins this app
content: I’ve used discord since the start of 2018 and I’ve gone through all the ups and downs of this platform, but throughout the entire course of using it, this is the first time I’m considering completely abandoning it and getting all my friends to make the switch to something like Guilded. The UI has changed almost entirely, the backdrop color changed from a easy on the eyes grey to an extremely harsh dark blue. You can no longer swipe left to see the members list, now you must press on the search icon (for God knows why??) to see it and then it seems there’s no way to exit that screen other than jumping to a message someone sent or that was pinned. Instead, swiping left now replies to messages, which is very unnecessary as you can just hold tap on a message and press reply—very little of the time do I actually need to reply to a message to even need a quicker action for it, as most conversations flow naturally with very few uses of the reply feature. The friends list has been moved completely, which isn’t the worst thing, but it’s just more inconvenient and unnecessary. I haven’t tried streaming or voice calls yet since this change, but I imagine they’ve been messed with as well. Frankly, the app just makes me feel incredibly claustrophobic now and it’s so infuriating to use now. If they reverse the UI update, I will bump this up to 5 stars, as the app has been great until now.
author: LeEpicDoge27

title: Big problems for motion sensitivity.
content: I use discord on mobile because it's often inconvenient to get to a PC, and while it is adequate for sending a message in a pinch; there are some meaningful shortcomings. I am someone who is sensitive to things moving on my phone screen outside my control. I needs gifs to not autoplay, and if the screen jumps around at random, it is stressful, almost painful. On gifs, fortunately discord delivers. Unfortunately, it does so by disabling gifs entirely. Even when I tap on a gif to look at it, it still doesn't play 90% of the time, so in exchange for having a useable client, I can't see the contents of a gif, even when I want to. That's problem number one. The big issue comes up when I want to read a message in a channel in which users are actively posting. Every time a message comes in, my scroll position in the channel moves wildly, up or down, seemingly at random. It makes it literally impossible to read anything in a channel, unless the channel has no current activity. This to me is unacceptable. At no point should I be interrupted from reading something by the text suddenly moving, let alone moving entire page-lengths off of the screen in an unpredictable direction. This has been an issue for years, and somehow it has never been addressed. Gives the impression that the mobile client, and accessibility, are not priorities.

author: BooperDooper999

title: Great Website!
content:
Discord has been incredible for me, I have been able to talk to and call friends, connect with new people, and it all has been very private and  secure. 
At first, I was a little bit superstitious when it came to discord. It did seem like a very open messaging service, leading to incidents with cyber bullies/child predators. Since getting discord, all of these worries have basically vanished. It is a high quality messaging and calling service (especially for large groups), and it can also serve as a way to meet new people. In my experience, I have stayed on private servers and direct messages with my friends, but I have still gotten a ton of usage out of the app. 
I highly recommend this app to anyone looking for a nice voice calling or messaging service. I would also like to mention to any parents who are nervous to allow their kids to use this to at least give it a chance. If your child stays in groups with just his friends, they will be absolutely safe, and if they do go into a public server, I have found that people are generally very nice. Plus, if you do get into a situation that is uncomfortable, you can simply leave the group or block the caller. 
I hope this helps!
author: Deco_Urchin

title: Every Update makes everything worse
content:
I use this app all the time. I’d rate it 5 stars. But something that makes me infuriatingly mad every time is when I update discord, they change every piece of UI, every color, every location where a button used to be, every font, and it ALWAYS is worse. I don’t know how you can make so many bad changes in a row. It seems statistically unlikely but discord pulls through every time to deliver the worst product possible.

Awhile back I started getting notifications every time anyone I was friends with changed their profile picture or status. It wasn’t possible to turn those off without updating. So I updated and I wish I didn’t. I wish I just turned off all notifications for discord. That would be a better solution. Because now all the buttons are in different places. It takes more clicks to get to the settings menu. I can’t find my inbox. The colors are garish and the high contrast hurts my eyes. There are more buttons and tabs that I will never use taking up screen space. I had just gotten used to the fact that you had to scroll up for the search bar to appear, and now it’s a permanent fixture, taking up space? Seriously! What were you guys thinking? 
The colors are my biggest issue. I don’t even want a fancy multi-color nitro background. I just want a grey background between light and dark. The App Store has more pleasant UI than you, discord. Do better.
author: Q4hehe

title: Consistently worse with each update serious privacy issues.
content:
I use discord 15+ hours a day and I will say that the mobile version for the iPhone is incredibly broken. I have been using discord on iOS for over a year now and every update it gets worse. The app will consistently mute and unmute me while my phone is across the room, mid conversation. If I have my headphones in and I get a phone call, it will unmute me in discord with no notification sound whatsoever. The number of times that I have had full conversations with people in my household, being completely unaware that everyone in discord could hear me because the app decided to unmute me, is ridiculously high. Half the time I open the app the audio output setting to change to the speakerphone is not even visible or available as a drop-down option and I have to force close the application, or completely restart my phone in order to get the speaker option to appear. The app consistently tries to switch to my mobile data, even though I am in my house with 100% Wi-Fi coverage. I have no issues with any other app, whether I’m using my headphones or not, and no issues with any other app losing signal, but discord is consistently unable to function on a basic level.

I am using a brand new iPhone, and without being able to replicate these issues through any other app, on top of hearing all of my friends in discord who use iPhones complain about the same issues on a daily basis, it’s apparent that the app has serious issues. The privacy issue with the app unmuting on its own, randomly, is a serious concern.
author: JBWainwright

title: I really love this app
content:
I absolutely love Discord because it’s the perfect platform for staying connected with my friends, family, and communities. Whether I’m chatting with close friends in private voice channels or hanging out with like-minded people in public servers, it feels like a place where I can truly be myself. The ease of use and versatility of Discord are unmatched whether I’m gaming, collaborating on a project, or just catching up on life, the experience is seamless. I can drop into a conversation at any time, knowing that there are so many ways to communicate, whether through text, voice, or video. 

What really makes Discord stand out is the way it blends socializing with customization. From creating my own servers to tweaking settings for a more personalized experience, there’s so much flexibility in how I organize my interactions. The ability to create channels for specific topics or interests means I can keep conversations organized and clutter-free. Plus, the bots, integrations, and unique features like screen sharing or live streaming make it even more enjoyable. Discord isn't just a chat app it's a community hub, and it’s become an essential part of how I connect, learn, and share with others. ❤️

author: angxlics

title: Near Invaluable
content: Since I joined my first server, it took some time for me to get used to all the functionality. There were so many things I didn’t know about, and yet that’s one of Discord’s biggest selling points. Most of the time if you want to do something, you can. Mark a server or channel as NSFW or 18+? You can do that. Change your display name for only one, specific server? You can do that too. But for me the most valuable thing about Discord is the sense of community that you feel almost immediately after logging on. Depending on your server choices you’ll almost always have an unread message, meaning there’s almost always something or someone for you to come back to. And if you don’t want to be bothered? Turn off notifications for servers and channels you don’t want to hear from. Not once have I had a security issue or even fear that I would lose personal information. Setting up 2-factor authentication was the easiest security experience I have had in a long time, and if you still have concerns, you won’t be required to even give Discord your phone number,  much less your name and other personal info. When I’m not using the in-built messages app on my phone or tablet, Discord is my #1 default
author: BluChange

title: Latest UI Design & Changes Continue to Disappoint
content:
It's all in the title. These UI changes to both the desktop and mobile versions have been terrible. Mobile Discord UI in particular has taken some extremely heavy hits in UI redesign that did NOT need to happen. I manage a few servers with as few as 10 to a couple hundred people and being able to navigate, edit permissions for channels/users/server/etc., access direct messages, review/open/close/edit threads, etc. on the go are highly important. The changes to tap and swipe on the mobile app makes these gestures counterintuitive and are costing myself (and others) to waste so much time trying to get or do what we actually intended to do. The UI did not need these changes and these changes do not serve to provide the user with a better experience. As these poor decisions continue to be made and do not seem to stop or be rolled back, I am looking for alternatives and will be migrating my communities off of Discord ASAP.

UPDATE: Downgraded my review by 1 star to the lowest rating due to the developer's response that lacks accountability for poor decision making and understanding of what the issues discussed are. Refusal to admit you made bad, unwanted, and very poorly received changes to a previously functional and intuitive UI is not a good look nor inspires confidence in the developer's ability to resolve such issues or make innovative changes to the app.
author: Asmodeí

title: Good, but message requests is aggravating
content:
Overall, discord is a good app to keep in touch with my friends, especially as we’ve stopped playing the games we’ve met in or fallen off other social media sites! It’s an alright platform for us F2P folks since none of us particularly NEED extra emojis and it’s really just for communication (although I’ll admit the video length threshold is a little low, I think most people consider a “short” video to be about Vine length)

But this “message requests” thing is AWFUL. I was told it was a newer thing, but I’d like to be able to set my messages to just “if you’re in my servers you’re probably messaging me for a reason, approved automatically”.  I’m sure you’re trying to protect me but I can block anyone being annoying pretty easily.  Or, at the very least, let the message requests NOTIFY me I HAVE a request.  The pm icon doesn’t pop up an alert at ALL and there’s no request push notification either.  It’s a pretty good way to miss someone in your server messaging you about time-sensitive stuff and it’s really not helpful if you’re the unlikely-to-message-first-unless-they-do introvert sort :( If there could be a fix on the notifications for it, or a setting that bypasses it, that would be great!
author: Brenna of House Targaryen

author: x_shadix

title: Wonderful app from a member of the Discord Role-play Community!
content:
Honestly, this app is what gets me through a lot of boredom in my day. It’s great, and even on the occasions there’s a problem, the devs tend to fix it rapidly with surprising speed. I use Discord to Role-play a lot, in fact it’s become my favorite pass time for the last year or so. The only thing I kind of wish was a bit better, is the character limit.

As a member of a few role-play servers I find myself often constricted by the 2000 character limit, especially considering I tend to write out 10K+ messages in google docs that I then post for characters that I role-play. As I’m sure is obvious, when I do several of these posts an hour the process of copying and pasting fragments of the messages becomes tedious. Not something that I generally hate, because with how wonderful discord servers are, allowing for many channels to be set up in ways that allow role-play servers to set up several settings, the limited characters per message is far outweighed in my preference. But, in a future update, if at all possible, I’m sure I, and the large amount of Novella Role-play members would certainly enjoy and appreciate an extended or unlimited message character limit.
author: Opus' Sepulchre

title: Updates and changes
content: Not that I believe this will be seen by the right people, but I seriously hope that the discord team is seeing the outcry for many of its users. After the most recent update for mobile, the app has become almost completely unusable for those who run massive servers or use the app as their only way of communication. Taking away the simple swipe of the side bar has been probably the most problematic and annoying part about this change, and one I pray will be added back soon. However, for those who manage servers and can’t get to where their going quick enough— this feature feels clanky and uncomfortable. The search feature as well, hardly works like it’s supposed to. You wanted to look for a gif in an ongoing conversation? Be prepared for it to cover your whole screen, then by the time you’re already picking one, you’ve gone and sent it at an inappropriate time because the conversation moved on without you knowing. The messages, sure, I can give the benefit of the doubt that they work like iMessages now, but the eyesore it is to open the message tab up and see everything crammed there is pretty uncomfortable and annoying. At least with the old features you didn’t have to open every message when clicking on messages— you’d just see their icon. Overall, I believe discord should be a place where people come to gather and express themselves, and the one thing that made discord stand out was their accessibility and easygoing style of layout. Now that it has changed so dramatically, I truly hope that the discord teams will hear their communities voices and meet us half way.

author: bonnie from splatoin 2

title: This new UI…
content: TLDR: The app is great, the new UI is not. I absolutely adore Discord and I’ve been using it for 4 years, so I’m going to try my best to write a quality review that is detailed and helpful. I just got hit with the update for the new UI, I’ve been dreading. This for awhile due to the things I have heard from fellow discord users. And I have to say, they weren’t exaggerating. After picking my theme, the first thing I noticed is how bubbly and clumsy it is. Everything feels very blown up making it difficult to type and navigate servers. When I try to scroll up and down to read chat, I find myself accidentally swiping to reply to messages. Next, the dms. I find it very difficult to navigate as they are not above the servers, this was much preferable to them having their own tab. I very much dislike that the dms take up the whole screen and the last message sent is shown, this makes it difficult to keep private messages private. This also means that less dms are shown so I have to do a lot more scrolling. Time for the mentions tab. There isn’t much I have to say about it other than I wish the mentions, activity feed, and things like accepted friend requests had different tabs like before. I dislike all the round corners and much prefer the previous ones, being sharp and square. This was much more visually pleasing to me. Now for the pros. I find myself enjoying that the friends portion now has separations between the letters ie a b c d. I also enjoy how the editing status and profile is more obvious and simple. Overall, I wish I could reverse the update and go back to the previous UI or have the option to switch between the two as I recognize that some people might enjoy this new UI.

author: Fluttershy311

title: Image transparency no longer works as of recent updates (my patience with this app is being tested)
content:
As an artist, I like to use Discord as my main messaging platform for both friends and clients due to its convenience and widespread usage. However, recent updates have made this difficult for two glaringly apparent reasons.

I’m not certain when exactly this began, but a recent update somehow “broke” image uploads for mobile users — PNGs and other static images that should be high quality and transparent are now given white backgrounds and visible compression artifacts. This is not an issue when sending comedic images, but it absolutely is when sending artwork to my clients. I’ve had to upload them elsewhere and link to them to preserve their intended quality, which is inconvenient and infuriating. A chat platform that I once counted on for keeping my images intact has somehow degraded to the likes of social media platforms I’ve abandoned partially due to similar reasons; I should not have to upload my art elsewhere if Discord is able to handle uploading the same images from desktop without running into compression/transparency issues.

I’ve used this app for nearly a decade now. I have sung its praises endlessly. I have paid for a full Discord Nitro subscription for several years without interruption. However, I cannot tolerate the half-baked, feature-breaking updates that have been pushed out more frequently over the years, even ruining the user experience for actual customers. If it continues to destroy itself in this way, I will be able to say I no longer recommend it. For now, I will just say it is getting harder to support the app’s development.

author: Frost Ashdove

title: Easy to navigate
content:
Discord mobile makes it quick and easy to navigate through servers, respond to messages, update your profile, make calls, organize your servers, and more with only one hand.
The *only* downsides to choosing mobile over desktop would have to be creation and moderation of servers being quite difficult, and receiving push notifications. 
When it comes to server creation, I found many options to be desktop-only. That, or near impossible to find. As for push notifications, they seem to occasionally entirely disappear and after a bunch of troubleshooting, the only solution has been to delete and reinstall the app. It happens a ton more if you are one to switch between browser and mobile often. An unfortunate and common issue for mobile users, but we can only hope it will be fixed in a future update. 
Overall, discord mobile is a secure and convenient way to communicate with friends and connect with others online. It’s an essential app on my phone and I use it more than any other messaging app. If you’re considering downloading it, I highly recommend doing so!

Grass has several functions. We cannot digest it and yet it is one of the most important resources for our food production: animals eat grass and we eat animal products such as meat, eggs and milk. Furthermore, we also use grass in other ways: for sport, recreation and to brighten up gardens and public spaces. This plant also has important ecological functions: it protects against soil erosion, it absorbs water, it purifies the air we breathe and so on.
 
Every variety of grass has its own special properties. The grass family, or Graminae, has about 8,000 varieties. There are suitable varieties of grass for cultivation at almost every temperature and every amount of rainfall. Some grasses can thrive during extreme drought because they have very long roots which can extract water from deep under the ground. Other sorts can flourish in extreme cold or withstand long periods of rain.
 
Most people take grass for granted but we shouldn't forget that grass plays a very important role in our lives. Scientists all over the world are working on research, improvement, breeding and cultivation of this very important crop. Barenbrug does this, too. But that isn't all that we do. author: Pomodoko

title: What Once Was Fun…
content:
…has now become far less so for me.

As a writer by hobby, I love using a Bluetooth keyboard with my iPad, making it easier to type up documents, messages and such without having to lose the tactile effect of a real keyboard. However, the most recent updates to this app, which I used to communicate with a small group of friends, have brought a crushing blow to my enjoyment of it. Up until recently, when using my Bluetooth keyboard, I could hit the “Enter” key to send messages, but now… now it only causes a line break into a new paragraph in a message, which used to be tied to the Shift+Enter combination exclusively. And there is no button in the settings menu of the iOS app to change this.

I could easily forgive if this update aspect had simply swapped the functions of Enter and Shift+Enter, but removing the “Enter to send” functionality entirely? No. This is an absolutely appalling decision on the part of the developers, and I would strongly urge them to change it back, or else give users the option to choose whether to use it or not, and/or to what key or key combination they would rather bind the function. Otherwise, many users who, like me, have developed a muscle memory to hit Enter to send messages will continue to have a problem with what was once a glorious app.

author: Dxalringg

title: the best thing about discord
content: Discord is an outstanding multimedia messaging platform that transcends its gaming roots. Whether you’re strategizing with teammates or simply chatting with friends, Discord offers a seamless experience across text, audio, and video communication. Here’s why it’s a must-have: It lets you create free public or private servers, making it easy to connect with friends or strangers. It works seamlessly across computers, mobile devices, and game consoles. While it’s not specifically marketed for enterprise-level security, Discord’s end-to-end encryption ensures privacy for your messages. Organize and customize your server to suit your needs. Whether you’re a gamer, hobbyist, or professional, Discord adapts. Discord Nitro offers premium features like custom emotes, animated avatars, and larger file uploads. Even the free tier provides ample functionality. When members boost a server, it levels up, unlocking premium benefits. Discord’s popularity extends beyond gamers, making it an Editors’ Choice winner for online messaging tools. In summary, Discord bridges communication gaps, fosters communities, and adds a touch of fun to your digital interactions.

author: Yip yip yooray

title: Quality App
content:
Discord has always been a friend of mine. When I first began gaming on Steam in late 2015, I used Skype. But it quickly became clear that Discord was a much higher quality alternative. For a price of nothing this app accomplishes a lot and demonstrates the quality and integrity of Hammer and Chisel. Everything from the non chinglish description to the actual, human written developer responses emanates a down-to-earth feeling about Hammer and Chisel. There's nothing that makes me happier than a development team that represents the antithesis of everything we've seen recently on the App Store. Thousands of apps that all do the same thing, written by Chinese and Indian companies attempting to either scam you or take your money. Discord is not one of those. This app was written well, and has not lagged at all on my iPhone 6+. It even features skillfully coded transitions to segments, making it fully compliant with Apple's new HIG (Human Interface Guidelines). It's people like those at Hammer and Chisel that make the world a better place for everyone, and I salute you. Keep on doing what you're doing now, and never give in to the pressures of advertisements and information-selling. This app is also a great place to find new friends and communities. It was through discord that I made many of my online friends and where I strengthened many existing friendships. It was there that I learned how to be a staff member and deal with troublemakers in a responsible way. This type of experience is invaluable for teenagers like myself as it serves as a preparation for careers and how to behave in a workplace. No matter why you're here, I can safely say you will enjoy the journey you have on Discord.

Thanks for reading, and have a great day.

content:

Could use a redesign.  Like why isn’t voice just enable in the same chat room so there’s no switching back and forth?

author: Ezephel Roman

title: A company willing to risk everything and everyone to gain nothing but hallow honor
content: If you haven’t heard or seen the press release yet, discord in its infinite wisdom is setting all accounts to “teen” by default sometime march 2026. This platform has been a lifeboat of culture, community, and companionship for several years now and is choosing to burn all that good will and positive public support to put its own consumer base at risk. Best case if this is truly the path they’re committed to is that the platform is mostly left abandoned as cybersecurity experts advise against following the new mandate and another competitor slides in and we repeat this cycle. Worse case discord is hacked, AGAIN, and the data and IDS of millions of users are leaked into the dark web exposing whole populations to identify theft, and with the “teen” filter now the default bad actors work around moderation guidelines to send or receive harmful content to/from minors. Truly the golden age of social media is over and we are now entering a dark age where companies put their entire consumer base at risk just to appear like they care about protecting minors without actually asking who’s at risk here. The dangers and risks here don’t take a college degree in ethics or computer science to grasp; and what we have is a nightmare scenario waiting to play out. Discord is officially a red flag level 9 security risk. DO NOT DOWNLOAD!

title: Opening profiles while in a voice channel needs reverted

Now, you have to press and hold for an unknown amount of time, just some time that is deemed “long enough” defined in the UI design, and then the profile appears (with volume slider, individual mute button etc) on release of the press and hold. I don't understand the purpose of this mechanic, or if this is a bug, but it is definitely not something I enjoy having to deal with when I’m in a voice channel and need to access someones profile popup while in the channel. Otherwise, the app seems to still be well laid out. This was the primary thing I noticed that drastically changed and it is not a short timer for the press and hold as was previously. It is definitely longer, then this combined with the activate on release behavior makes this difficult to use.

author: Katiecatt1804805

title: Huge security risk
content:
I’ve been using Discord for a while, but the app has some serious issues that make it a headache to use. When I’m on a voice channel, it freezes way too often, locking me in the call with no way to disconnect unless I force close the app entirely. Worse, the app has this infuriating bug where it unmutes users repeatedly in the middle of a voice channel. It’s happened to me countless times—every time I get a phone call or open another app while listening in, it unmutes me without warning. This isn’t just a glitch; it’s a huge security risk, exposing private chats to anyone nearby. For an app built around communication, these problems are unacceptable. Until they fix this, it’s a 1-star experience for me. Avoid if you value reliability and privacy.

UX bug: Disruptive Chat Scrolling One of Discord’s most frustrating UX issues rears its head when scrolling through a chat page. As I’m reading or navigating older messages, the app suddenly jolts and jumps around whenever new messages are posted. This interrupts my scrolling experience, yanking me out of context and forcing me to lose my place. It’s not just jarring—it’s unnecessary. If I want to move, I can do it myself or choose to jump to the latest message. A simple fix, like locking the view until I opt to shift, would go a long way.

author: watchdogsunlimited

title: Discord was good when it was a messenger app, not social media
content:
I have been using discord basically since the beginning. It's gone through a lot of changes, and the vast majority have been tolerable, but the latest update has turned discord into an app I use solely because my friends do. If another messenger app came out, I'd swap in a heartbeat.
The extra dark background on dark mode is harsher against the white text. It causes eye strain.
The notifications tab, one of 4 tabs on the bottom bar, doesn't even get the badge when you get a notification. The badge shows up on either the server tab, or the DMs tab. Why even have a notifications tab if your notification badges don't show up there? If I wanted to find my previous mentions, I would use the search function and find "mentions: me". Easy! A whole tab for it is unnecessary.
It used to be easy to get from a server to DMs and back again. Just a swipe and a tap. Now you have to tap twice, swapping between tabs. You used to be able to see who was messaging you just by swiping to the side. You stayed where you were on whatever server you were in, you just now could see someone's profile pic and the notification badge with the amount of messages from them. Now you only see the number badge on the DMs tab. Just the number of how many total messages you have. You have to leave the server channel you're in to even see WHO messaged you, and then to get back to the server you'd better have turned off their "auto-enter into the homepage of this server" or else you'll have to go back to the channel you were in manually.
Discord is best when it is used for its actual purpose- text messaging and picture sending. Discord shouldn't be treated as a social media. If I wanted to go to social media, I'd go to reddit, or snapchat, or facebook, or anything else.

content:

content: Dear Discord Team, I hope this message finds you well. I have some suggestions that I believe could significantly enhance the user experience for server owners and members: 1. author: ThatOneGuy012

title: Great potential for adolescents if used safely
content:
The app is easy to use, especially on the desktop version. It allows users to really make the app what they want. They can use the app as a very social experience that ensures their connections to friends, even in such a secluded time of COVID. But users can also use it as an individual experience and can find others online who are interested in similar topics. The app's design is excellent, and I had a lot of fun playing around with the different settings and searching through the public communities with topics ranging from mental health to memeology. It is set up like Slack, so I could easily engage and explore because of my experience with that app. I also think it’s great that the user’s profile can be fully customizable and doesn’t come from an option list of user settings, such a pre-selected avatar pictures. Scanning the app, it seems like users can use their creativity with their profile and can use a real picture of themselves or just a meme with no identifying information. 

The weaknesses of the app include its accessibility and its privacy settings. There was no specific mention of accessibility, so it may be difficult to use the app if the user experiences vision disability or something similar. Also, while a user can opt out of certain cookies, there is no way to do a blanket opt out of the app's privacy collection processes. I also didn't like that I couldn't see possible friends that could already have a Discord account because there was no connection to my phone contacts or my contacts from any other social media account. However, I can also see the argument for this being a positive because it can be a completely separate program from all other apps the user uses, which is difficult to find sometimes because of the merging tech companies.
author: sarcampb

title: The worst form of social media
content:
Out of all of the social media platforms I’ve tried, discord I would say is the most toxic of them. 
And it’s not because the employees and staff working at discord are mean, or anything, it’s because of the nature of the setup discord chooses to use. Essentially when you join a server, the guidelines you have are the ones the owner sets for you. Larger servers are often governed by mods. But the problem is that these mods generally don’t have too many qualifications to be a moderator. And when the mods are ineffective at creating a safe environment, that’s when toxic behavior thrives. Discord does have some policies, on its ToS but these are generally very simple rules, and are few and far between. I’ve had many terrible experiences on servers where toxic behavior is present and the mods either do nothing about it or they take the wrong course of action. Now this isn’t something discord has much control over, but rather design of the website in it’s entirety is flawed. I wouldn’t recommend this app to people who who are not in a healthy state of mind, or to anyone in general. However I guess discord works for some people and if you find that this style of social media works for you then by all means download it. But do be prepared for possible toxic behavior thrown your way.

title: The fantasies and the depths
content: My journey with discord is not one of joy and happiness, but rather of despair and sorrow. Quarantine was where it began, virus infecting the land. Soon after, he realized this reliance on discord was a hindrance to himself. The connections he had made, once his pride and joy, was now nothing more than an obstacle, holding him back from attaining  what he really needed in life. It was in 2023, when he finally realized that this had to stop. Discord, an app for alleviating the discord in his life, was bringing him too much discord for him to function properly. To this day, he doesn’t regret meeting discord, rather instead regretting the reliance he put on it.

author: ZenMagus

title: Please never change, I love you too much
content:
What can I say about Discord? I started using it a year or so ago off of a friends recommendation, and I have no interest in going back to any of the multiple VOIP programs I’ve used in the past (Xfire, Skype, C3, Steam, Mumble, Teamspeak, Razer Comms); Discord beats out all of those for one major reason: Absolute control over everything. The ability to create and manage my own channel with access to just about every detail keeps me coming back, and makes things so much easier on me. Volume sliders on everybody giving me peace of mind on how loud (or quiet) people are being, being able to voice/text mute people that are being abusive in chat, and having multiple text/voice channels is just icing on the cake.

I told myself I wouldn’t write a review for Discord till they rolled out with the video call/screenshare update on PC, and they did so here I am. 

If you’re wanting a reliable, free, all-access VOIP program for your gaming or chatting needs, Discord is for you. With their optional Discord Nitro subscription offer I hope they never run out of money to support this gem.

title: As a server mod:
content: Discord is good at what is meant for: a chat program. Join servers, discuss in channels, and send private messages, talk in voice chat. However, they keep adding features that aren't necessary in order to make themselves a one-stop-shop social media despite the siloed nature of servers, and they're too eager to jump on the techbro scam bandwagons like NFTs. Many new features are added without consideration for user impact, such as loud noises from soundboards or flashing lights and colors from animations that can harm some disabled users. Many times it's difficult or even impossible to minimize or turn off features, personally or in one's server. As of this review, they just added a mandatory 3rd party app that allows users to "remix" anyone's posted images via generative AI. There is NO way to shut this off on a personal account level, nor can moderators choose not to have it in their server. The "Disable" feature only ensures the "remix" is sent privately instead. These new features should NEVER be automatic, they must be Opt In only and with ways to disable and disallow them. Discord needs to consider the users before getting hooked in by their own shiny new toys they want to force on everyone, whether anyone wants them or not.

title: Bad customer support
content:
I have had discord for 5+ years now and throughout those years I have joined a lot of servers and made a lot of online friends. It was a great way to enjoy gaming with other people that liked what I liked. However this year, March 4th 2022, my account was disabled with no warning or anything, just a email informing me. The email contained what “I had done” but never provides proof or evidence, because I have never posted or joined a server for revenge p***. Regardless I tried getting to customer support and OH BOY WAS THAT BAD. Instead of contacting you with someone, ie a HUMAN, they use bots for everything, including for disabling accounts. I get it’s a easy system to target accounts who violate the TOS and other bots/scammers and it would be hard to handle millions of users, but when people have given time and money to the platform for years you’d think they would review it personally or give a warning. Remember I DIDNT ANYTHING THEY CLAIMED IN THE EMAIL. Anyways after trying to appeal and getting denied by a bot, “shocker”, I gave up cause they don’t care about their individual consumers. I wish they had taken time to contact me and we can sort this out but unfortunately that will never happen. 

Also they “claim” after being disabled for 2 weeks your account will be deleted. But the few people I was able to keep in contact with say they can still see my account. I am also still being charged for nitro so if they could stop that or give me my account back I’d appreciate it. 

If you want to download Discord, go ahead but be careful of the servers you join and check them monthly to make sure they aren’t shady. Otherwise you’ll be taken out like I was without warning.

.....  I do have some complaints, though.  It is so hard for me to figure out how to do almost anything!  Over the years, the developers have made numerous updates... but never, it seems, toward making basic functions more user-friendly. It’s as if they cannot believe anyone would not find the learning curve a joy.
..... I realize that I am slower than a lot of people to learn things with computer programs. But I also notice that no one in our group, if they do know how to do something, has ever found it easy to explain how to do it to others.

title: Discord is a great app to enjoy talking to friends and others.
content:
In my opinion, yes. I’ve made lots of friends on Discord and I speak to them everyday. Find a server or community that shares your interests and bond with others. Speak to others from around the world and share your opinions on things you like.

As on all chatting platforms or social media, please be careful about your personal information. There are some weirdos, trolls, and there might even be some pedophiles. My friend, unfortunately, was preyed on by one of them.

However, don’t make that turn your back away from Discord. I only said the above to warn you in case anything should happen, which I hope not. In that case, you should report and block immediately. author: ThePotatoPringle

title: The new interface is terrible
content:
The latest update completely redid the UI without any warning (the app store update notes literally just gave the same rote "bug fixes and performance enhancements"
with no warning that the update would completely upend and ruin the app), and all of it feels like "Change made for the sake of change and trying to become yet another duplicate of every other social media app" instead of actually looking at how people who use Discord want to use Discord.
The layout now no longer matches the desktop app, which forces my brain to stop and consciously hunt for things every time I switch to my phone, instead of just effortlessly bouncing between them. The new dark mode colors are harsh and painful to read on (and just unpleasantly ugly). The new "Messages" page inexplicably adds a screen-space-blocking box of friends' activity (which nobody wants or asked for) that forces you to scroll further when trying to actually look through your messages (like,the actual reason for going into an area labeled "Messages"), and with no way to turn off that unwanted Activity section. The press-and-hold menus for posts and servers now take up twice as much space and give half as many options. The extra separate button for servers instead of just swiping from the left means the bottom menu is claustrophobically crowded if you're still using a smaller phone. Images no longer show up in pinned messages, meaning you have to click through to the message (which defeats the entire point of pinning it!).

author: Theedie

title: UI changes and the unfriendly behavior discord shows to its users
content: Discord's recent UI changes have indeed triggered widespread discontent among users, especially with the overhaul of features like the search function and pins. Notably, users now face the inconvenience of missing image previews in search results and pins, having to click through to view them. The absence of a preview and the "jump to message" function adds to the frustration, abruptly sending users to the selected message without a preview option. The lack of saved positions within the pins/search section exacerbates the user experience, necessitating repeated scrolling. The new unified list without page separation and the absence of auto-completed search filters further complicate the once-intuitive search process. Users also lament the removal of the swipe-to-view members list feature, now replaced by the need to click on the channel name for access. These changes collectively contribute to a perception of Discord's UI becoming less user-friendly and more cumbersome in its recent updates. Moreover, Discord's decision to abandon elements that once made it unique—specifically, its simplicity and informal vibe—has further fueled user discontent. The platform's charm lay in its less corporate feel, providing a casual and user-friendly environment for communities to thrive. However, recent UI changes seem to be pushing Discord towards a more corporate aesthetic, diminishing the simplicity that endeared it to users. This shift in design philosophy raises concerns among the user base, as they perceive Discord moving away from its roots and losing the distinctive qualities that set it apart from more formal communication platforms.

author: Hyoasei

title: New UI
content:
The new UI isn’t very good. It feels much slower to navigate, and I don’t like having a separate messages tab, because when everything was in one place before it felt much easier. My main problem is just that there isn’t an option to use the old UI anymore. In previous iterations of the new UI, this feature was available, so nobody was forced into it, and could keep using the old UI like before. Please add this back so that users such as myself can continue to use the old UI if they don’t like the new one.

I also feel like this UI change was unnecessary. There was nothing wrong with the old UI. Your site said that you wanted the mobile UI to feel optimized for mobile rather than a scaled down version of the desktop UI, but, for me at least, I use both versions, and them both having the same layout provides a consistency between the two that makes it easier to use. 

If you want to improve the UI, the best thing to do is to not change it at all, because “if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.” Or just make the new UI optional so that those who like it can use it and those who don’t can keep using the old one and feel more comfortable with the app.
author: vhhfvhivdntvdhul

title: New Layout Killed Functionality
content:
Discord has introduced a new UI layout that while very new, has a lot of features that kill the functionality of the site in comparison to the desktop versions. First, the new theme is harsher on the eyes for people who liked dark mode for accessibility versions. Second, it takes more clicks to get to certain pages, like finding activity and membership lists. Third, with the old UI you could automatically open on the conversation you were having, or if you got a direct message you could click on the profile bubble of your friend and be immediately taken to the conversation. Now it forcibly opens on the message page regardless of your last conversation, and now when you receive a DM you have to go to the messages page and open it. These may seem like small features, but make the layout feel more clunky and less optimized. Fourth, information is now hidden in places like pinned messages, where you can’t see images or previews of the messages which is what made the feature useful in the first place. 
I’m tempted to uninstall the app and find an alternative version to use. Don’t get discord until something changes.

author: Blake598

title: DISCORD IS AMAZING!
content:
I haven’t written a review in probably over 10 years, this app is so amazing on ALL platforms that felt the need to tell everyone who hasn’t used this app to PLEASE give it a try. It has so many amazing features and I don’t even know where to start. Firstly, you can use Discord to call another user as if it were just a normal phone call or FaceTime call and the quality is amazing with or without WiFi, it works just fine even if it is ran only on data. Secondly, you can turn a one way call, into a three-way call, four-way call, five-way call, six-way etc, this app is perfect for talking to multiple people at once. You can create long term dedicated chat rooms that can be used for multiple things, you can create a room, name it, organize it with labeled tabs, create multiple chat channels of multiple topics in the same room, unique tabs for sending images, work related topics, video game related topics, meme channels for only sending memes, you can create a welcome tab for new members to view upon entering the room via invitation, you can add rules to each channel to ensure they are used for the purpose which they were created, you can have a voice channel and text channels for general usage such as normal conversation, you can have a private voice channel for one on one conversation, you can even customize your profile with a chosen name and image. The name can be any name you want and there is no confusion between profiles with the same name since they are primarily identified through a unique 4-5 digit number at the end of each name. You can add a profile picture and bio as well. 

There is so much more I haven’t even mentioned that is just as important if not more but if I brought up everything I would be typing all day. 

Overall, Discord is an amazing app. If you haven’t tried it then you should. It’s completely safe and the TOS is very strict about safety and ensuring that you have privacy with your personal info and conversations.
author: Mist Star

title: Deleting my account over data breech concerns
content: I’m really disappointed in Discords decision to require government IDs or use of our biometric data if it’s unable to “passively verify” our age. I’ve gone down a few rabbit holes since learning about this decision, trying to convince myself to stay, and I’ve come to the conclusion that I’m not confident I can trust Discord’s ability or willingness to protect our data. We live in a world where a lot of  concerning things are being normalized: from our data being harvested for training AI models whose data centers ultimately draining our supply of available drinking water… to biometric theft and mass surveillance, just to name a few. While I appreciated learning that the 3rd party service being used for age verification wasn’t part of the recent data breach that leaked 10s of thousands of users data, I’m concerned about the probability of this happening again. I also find the notion of “passive verification” to be more than a little creepy. I understand that is likely the current state or trajectory of most big tech companies, I just had this naive idea that Discord would be going in a different direction. In light of all this, I will unfortunately be deleting my account.

title: New Layout (12/23)
content:
I’ve been an avid Discord fan for years. It’s been a great way to keep up with friends and look at cute cat photos. The new layout is inaccessible (for one thing, newly oversaturated dark mode backgrounds that make it hard to read the light text) and removes a lot of the many features that made Discord so beloved by users, such as having direct messages at the top left of the screen for easy access (which are now in another tab entirely, making it tedious to switch between servers and direct messages). The list goes on.

Discord staff claimed before the update that there would be an option for users to opt out of the new layouts, at least initially. They were untruthful when they said this; such an option has not been added. I know I’m not alone in feeling this way; every user I’ve spoken to (and many more outside my own communities and circles whom I’ve never met) has been upset with the new change and is frustrated with Discord for not listening to its user base. 

I hope developers take notice and do something about this issue, but I’m not super hopeful. It’s sad to see one of my favorite apps go this direction and I may start looking for alternatives :(

author: Kenriquez04

title: New UI - Unintuitive and Inaccessible
content: Opening up discord today I see “An improved mobile experience has arrived!” and I think to myself “Okay cool, a new update!” and swipe up to see what has changed. First thing I notice is the new colors for dark mode, I don’t like it, but I assume I can change it back in a bit. While looking around at all the new changes, which I will discuss soon, I begin to develop a headache. This is due to my astigmatism, the drastic contrast of white text on the almost black background creates a vividly bright blooming affect that strains my eyes whenever looking at the screen. I quickly go to settings to change this eyesore and notice there is no option to switch back! I try light mode, but that isn’t much better. Every time I get on the app now I am left with a headache, and I cannot imagine what it’s like for people with worse conditions. Another issue I have is the inability to simply swipe and see server lists. I now have to use my other hand and tap the channel name, which is much more inconvenient and unintuitive than before. Technology is supposed to be designed for convenience, and this change is less convenient and inaccessible for people who say only have one hand or those who are using their other one for something else. There was no reason for a lot of these UI changes! I feel like they were made to appease investors who want to see growth on the platform, but Discord is very niche, you aren’t going to see older people join when they have other apps like Facebook. You need to appease your already strong user base, and these changes have a lot of us enraged. They say growth for the sake of growth is the philosophy of a cancer cell. Keep that in mind when you make useless changes to “grow” your user base, this will put you behind in the long run.

title: Discord has ruined everything, very quickly
content:

I struggle to comprehend the rationale behind the alterations, and attempting to pinpoint and articulate the multitude of issues has proven to be a daunting task.

It is my sincere hope that Discord takes into serious consideration the community's feedback and explores three potential courses of action. Firstly, a rollback of the update could be a viable solution, reinstating the previous version that users found more agreeable. Alternatively, providing an option to revert to the older interface could cater to the diverse preferences within the user base. Lastly, a prompt and effective resolution of the usability concerns is imperative, ensuring that the platform becomes functional and user-friendly once more.

Despite my genuine affection for Discord, the current state of the application is disheartening enough for me to take a stand. Until these issues are adequately addressed and rectified, I have decided to uninstall the application. Rest assured, I plan to revisit and update my review once the necessary improvements have been implemented.

title: Upcoming changes are unconscionable
content:
If I was judging the current functionality and experience of the app, it would be around 4 stars. However, the decision to implement a worldwide requirement to either use a face scan or government ID, literally just months after implementing the same thing in one country and having that information immediately get hacked and leaked, when you had promised over and over before the implementation that said verification data would not be stored, is such a head-in-the-sand move that it would be funny if it wasn't so dangerous for so many people and their personal data. And we know that the real reason doesn't have anything to do with protecting children; the real reason is because the company just recently secretly filed for an IPO and wants to look good for shareholders in terms of how much data they have and can collect to sell, train AI models on, and all the things that shareholders love.

The direction of the app and the experience as a user had frankly been declining steadily for several years, especially as paid cosmetic features and Quests were more and more aggressively shoved down the user's throat over time. So the functionality and experience I mentioned above has already declined to be around 4-star worthy, instead of the easy 5 it once used to be. But these decisions made recently have been enough that I have canceled my Nitro and all server boosts after almost 7 years of very loyal patronage, and will be encouraging my friends and others to do the same, then migrate over to some other alternative, even one that may not be as fully featured. The direction of the company and service simply cannot be trusted anymore.

I've rated the app 2 stars for the time being because the functionality is still at a very high level for the time being, but once the changes are fully implemented I will change it to a one star review as deserved.

title: Great but missing key feature
