author: That one random review

title: Parent Alert!!!
content: This is NOT an app you want any child under 16 to have free access to...especially if you are not tech savvy.  Basically, you are allowing your child to chat with anyone.  I discovered some of the direct messages that were being sent to my son and they were completely toxic....memes about where to hide a knife at school, disturbing images, explicit content.  Oh, and some of the other  “friends” he was chatting with talked about how their parents just thought they were only communicating with other kids from school.  Do not fall for it parents!   There is one thing you can do (which I wish I had realized to do sooner) and that is only YOU, the parent, have the password.  Go into Privacy settings and set it so that no one can direct message your child, no friend requests etc.  If your child has the password, they will just change the settings back.  Make a condition of using it that your child doesn’t get the password.  Then they will have to ask you before adding anyone as a friend.  You will also be able to monitor everything they are doing which, sadly, you 100 percent need to do with this site.

author: Eagle-P

title: New Feature Request
content:
I’ve been using discord for years now since I was a teen and I love using it, though an issue I’ve come across recently is hackers or certain scenarios occurring which result in deleting channels and categories that have a lot of history or important info within them that’s needed, which is why I believe a new feature could be made to help with the damaged.

An undo feature(similar to google docs) would be very useful in my opinion, where once a category or channel has been deleted, there is a time limit of at-least 30 days for it to be restored before the information is permanently deleted. This feature could be added in by making it so whenever someone presses the reorder button (by going through settings-channels and pressing the reorder button on the top right), a 4th option will show up that either says undo or restore, in which it’ll show recently deleted categories and channels that were deleted and also show how much time is left before its forever deleted. You can either choose to restore one at a time or select them all by dragging your finger down from the first category/channel you wish to restore and all the way to the bottom, in which you can press restore again(which can replace the reorder button for this since it’ll be showing a new screen without the already existing channels and categories) to restore any and all categories and channels that have been selected. 

I’d imagine it’ll take a certain amount of time for it all to be restored depending on how many was deleted, and possibly a limit on how many can be restored at a time, but I believe adding this feature could be a very beneficial addition to discord that many people could benefit from, especially largely-moderately populated servers that experience troubles among their own server members such as hackers and such. So please consider adding this feature to discord, I understand the possibility of this feature taking a-lot of time and effort to be implemented, but I do truly believe that it could help. If you’ve reached the end then I thank you for reading this review, and please consider this.

title: A bad habit
content:
As a longtime user, Discord got popular by a lot of coincidences, and has a bad habit of falling into every tech company's trappings as a result. The history of the program and later app involves a stunning amount of trial and error, yet a continued refusal to be up front about the errors. It's not the fault of any individual who might read this, but it's really an app we use because we have to, not out of preference. I used to support it and stopped because of these failings; I've never spent or even looked at the currently existing micro-transactions because they feel antithetical to the part I supported.

A captive audience isn't a loyal one, and eventually a poorly thought out decision like a games market, an nft system, a crypto market, and so on will stick and we'll find a new program, like we did with Skype. Unfortunately one of the best ways to encourage loyalty is also inconvenient, being transparent user-support communication. You know, so we would be able to give feedback without relying on private emails or third party review systems.

title: New Mobile Layout
content:
The most recent update has completely altered the way mobile works on Discord. It is not an inherently bad idea in itself, however, I and many others have complained about its features. Pinned messages do not show images nor full messages if they are long (without ANY indicator that there is more text added along with the said message), making pins ultimately useless. At the very least starboards can fix this issue, but in DMs, it is simply trash.

Additionally, the ease at which you can accidentally swipe off DMs/channels without the ability to switch back by pressing the server/messages button on the bottom tab is inconvenient. Rather than making these tabs do little emotes when double-tapped, why not have it so that double-tapping these will swipe it to the latest group chat/DM/channel?

DM pins are odd. Even if a message is pinned that *I* sent, it shows up as my DM partner’s message. Why? It’s stupid. 

Getting rid of the ability to search for messages before/after/during certain dates, in specific channels, mentions of certain users, and with specific embeds/links/files and making it a separate tab is inconvenient as well. If you wish to keep that, at the very least let users type “before:” and have the command WORK.

The links and files tab is also useless if you have a feature where you can search for links and files already. There is no point in having two tabs for that.

I have never had any issues with Discord glitching, crashing, nor have I experienced many bugs. Now, that is no longer the case—an incredibly frustrating discovery.

author: S¡nJi

title: Make the old discord interface an option again!
content:
In mid-2023, when Discord first started ringing alarm bells about a major update, I gave it a test run. I was horrified. The update I saw completely reconfigured the interface, removing the features I used the most and adding “features” that only served as distractions. This was a genuine accessibility problem for me. I tested the interface several times over the course of a month, but I was simply unable to get used to it. So just a couple days before Discord was due to update, I disabled automatic updates on my phone. I haven’t regretted it for a moment. I am aware that in the time since this update was first launched, Discord has modified that version I first saw to more closely resemble the one I use right now. However, the new interface still does not solve the accessibility issues I was worried about (I’ve tested it on others’ phones). So, Discord, despite your efforts to remove aspects of the app I had access to before the update, even though you’ve locked me out of playing games on calls and using soundboards and fancy text and hyperlinks, even though I can’t see polls and forwarded messages and games in chats, I will stand firm. You could strip every feature except calling and chatting and I would still not update. And if you ever tried to remove one of those, I would move on. I have no interest in supporting an app that willfully destroys accessibility for its users despite feedback and outright protest. The only way you will ever get a cent of my money is adding an option to use the old interface. In the meantime, I’ll ask for screenshots and play games on other services. Services that don’t think some nebulous vision of progress and modernity is more important than their users.
Edit after reply: the feedback site you’ve linked is so poorly designed that a full hour of searching and sifting through posts turned up nothing. I really don’t know why I expected otherwise.

author: Wolfkinzz

title: The only social app I enjoy
content:
The interface is clean, simple, and functional. but with the latest update, I have begun to dislike the direction it is going in.

The new text box is counter intuitive. It doesn't match the rectangular, in-line design format that the rest of the UI maintains. The gift icon has no reason to be right next to the image browser on mobile- why is it there? Buttons that are placed right next to each other should be related. I don't want to spend money on gifts NEARLY as often as I want to send a picture or an emoji in the chat.... it doesn't make sense. It makes it feel like a mobile game where there are ways to spend money around every corner. 

I beg of y'all not to start making everything round. EVERY other social app is round and soft and busy and all too friendly. Discord was just right- the simplicity of the design prioritized text-based conversations over anything else, which allowed for conversations to be easy to read, functional, and easy. Instagram and Twitter are dizzying apps with way too many features, and engagement/content is prioritized over conversation- that approach is far from what Discord's approach is, so it makes sense to me that y'all would avoid that visual language. 

pleeeease restore the prior, rectangular, text box interface. Finally, replies are convoluted. Replies feel clunky because they take up more vertical space... something to consider.

author: ChellyBelly888

title: Actually life changing
content:
I made a discord account back in late 2016, I started a server in early 2017. Thanks to a lot of amazing people it ballooned to nearly 500 members and turned into a full fledged community that is still thriving to this day. 

The point isn’t to brag (mostly) but to illustrate that my Discord server has become a permanent fixture in my life, I have met friends who are just as close to me as any other, it’s almost like a big online family, so much so that some of us have even met up in real life to hang out. The app has its issues but it’s frequently updated and so the utility of the app has massively inflated since I joined.

This review is honestly a bit of a mess and I’m probably not giving anyone any useful information. So my bottom line is essentially this: 

Discord is an incredibly versatile, functional, and easy to use app on both mobile and PC. It is distinctly aimed towards gamers, but it could be useful in just about any application you could need a social networking platform for. The developers possess an awesome sense of humor, and clearly care about the platform they’ve created. Don’t be put off by its reputation as having an entirely gamer-centric, younger demographic. Because as far as social networking goes, Discord has no equal in terms of functionality, it does everything you’d need for free, the premium account only does bonus features (like increased file size limit for file sharing), that are very useful, but don’t gimp the experience to not have in any significant way, especially for the cheap subscription. 

11/10 would allow it to consume my life again.

author: klyntarix

title: A great desktop & browser app, born for touch.
content:
I’ve cut my cord with TeamSpeak LONG AGO because that’s not how one should host real-time voice chat.  All my friends were transitioning from Skype to Discord when they first heard about it, so I did too.  I cannot say I’ve regretted that choice.

Discord is basically one of those apps/services that might seem boring or difficult from a screenshot, but it is such a simple and helpful tool that I use DAILY.  How is it this good?  It combines some of the most powerful features in regular text and voice communication into a free and easy-to-use app that you can view in a web browser or download on your computer/phone.  The experience doesn’t change, regardless.

The app itself is a slimmed-down version of the original desktop version, which the servers & channels and playerlists being in their own hidden panes.  This doesn’t hold me back at all. The app runs fast and is actively being improved all the time, with new TestFlight builds releasing every few days.

I can only think of one downside that doesn’t really affect my overall love for this program: when will there be a console version of the app we can download?

To conclude, it’s the best thing since online multiplayer.  It beats having to call a ton of people just to talk to a few.  And most of all, it beats having to pay for server hosting!

So if you’re ever looking for an app to find some people who you really get along with, try Discord. I’m being serious. I’d been in a sorta bad mental state for a few years. Felt like everyone pretty much hated me. Then I got discord and it felt like I belonged. I’m ok now, I can smile without forcing it. The whole reason I’m so much more social now than I have been is because of how much discord has helped my mental health. I wish I could put to words how much happier I’ve been lately, but I can’t. This is an honest recommendation here. I can’t make this up, honestly. If you want to try discord, then I definitely say go for it.

title: Updates ruined a good thing
content: Love the new dark mode, but now you can’t go a few days without Nitro being shoved at you one way or another. Direct messages and servers are separated star-crossed lovers who miss each other badly. The search function for DMs has gone into hiding. I peel the curtains back to find it cringing beside a friend’s profile. Have we hurt you so badly, that you need to look here for safety? There is clutter, there are ads, invasive AI stop to eavesdrop on your conversations.  I switch between servers, write out a message, switch again.  The screen is frozen.  Nothing loads.  I tap, tap, tap on the buttons, but they may as well be stoned.  This happens every so often.  I can try turning it off and back on again.  Surely I don’t expect any better?  And yet… I am haunted by the Discord that once was.  Where is the simple, clean layout we were lured by?  The fast, smooth model that did not crash every so often?  It is a distant memory, receding into a horizon we cannot see past all the Nitro promotions in our faces.

title: Doesn’t delete app data
content:
I hate having to do one star for this but I cannot begin to explain how frustrating this is. When you delete an app, it is supposed to delete all of your data for that app from your device; even though it prompts as if it will do that, unlike other apps, discord refuses to delete your data.

Em uma análise construtiva, acredito que seria importante reforçar as medidas contra interações criminosas, abusivas e degradantes dentro de grupos e servidores da plataforma. Diversos acontecimentos demonstram que usuários inocentes podem acabar sendo direcionados para ambientes inadequados, onde são enganados, manipulados ou expostos a situações prejudiciais.

Considero fundamental ampliar a fiscalização, a visibilidade e a rapidez na identificação desses comportamentos, bem como fortalecer os mecanismos de denúncia e proteção aos usuários. Essas medidas ajudariam a tornar a plataforma mais segura, 
reduzindo os riscos de exploração, assédio, golpes e outras atividades que violam as diretrizes da comunidade.

Meu objetivo com esta sugestão é contribuir para um ambiente mais seguro, transparente e acolhedor para todos os usuários

title: Melhorem!!!
content:
1. Áudio horrível
De todos os aplicativos que eu já usei na minha vida em que existe a possibilidade de gravar áudio, o Discord é disparado o pior. Parece que eu estou falando debaixo d’água.
O meu celular é bom, eu tenho um iPhone 12. Quando gravo áudio na câmera, no WhatsApp, no Instagram ou em qualquer outro aplicativo, o áudio sai ótimo. No Discord, porém, é extremamente ruim.
Isso chega a me desanimar de gravar áudios. Sem contar quando eu vou ouvir um áudio e quase não consigo, porque o som sai muito, muito baixo.
Além disso, o som só sai pela saída de cima do celular, a mesma usada para chamadas telefônicas. Pelo amor de Deus, isso precisa melhorar.

2. Câmera
Quando eu tiro uma foto diretamente pelo Discord, a qualidade parece a de um celular muito antigo, tipo um Samsung J5. Sério, por que isso acontece?
Quando vou gravar vídeos, a qualidade não é tão ruim assim, mas fotos são simplesmente terríveis.

3. Não é possível gravar áudio no computador
Como assim não dá para gravar áudio pelo computador? Pelo amor de Deus, isso não faz o menor sentido. É uma função básica que simplesmente não existe. Vocês precisam adicionar isso urgentemente.

4. Nitro
Esse sistema de Nitro é o cúmulo. O pior de tudo é não conseguir enviar arquivos por causa disso. Limitar uma função básica dessa forma é absurdo e extremamente frustrante.

title: O aplicativo é bom porém
content:
Dou 4 estrelas porque as missões e recompensas precisam ser muito mais equilibradas entre quem usa PC e quem usa apenas celular.

Para quem usa celular, aparecem poucas missões durante a semana. O mínimo que poderia ter seria umas 2 ou 3 missões por semana. Enquanto isso, para quem usa PC, aparecem várias, chegando facilmente a 5, 6 ou até 7 missões, o que acaba dando muito mais Orbs para quem joga no PC.

Não acho justo que os usuários de celular tenham tão poucas oportunidades de conseguir Orbs, principalmente quem assina o Nitro todos os meses. Parece que quem usa PC recebe muito mais benefícios e consegue acumular Orbs com muito mais facilidade, enquanto nós, usuários de iOS e Android, ficamos para trás.

Se o Discord quer incentivar os usuários a continuarem assinando o Nitro, deveria valorizar também quem usa o aplicativo exclusivamente pelo celular. Aumentem a quantidade de missões para usuários mobile e deixem as recompensas mais equilibradas para todos, independentemente da plataforma.

title: Beta
content:
The app itself is great, and the overall concept is excellent. However, it often feels like it’s still in a beta stage because of the sheer number of bugs and issues that keep occurring. Considering how expensive Nitro is, users should expect a much more stable and polished experience. An app with a premium subscription shouldn’t suffer from this many glitches and performance problems.

Additionally, the desktop application could be much lighter. Discord consumes an excessive amount of system resources and often ends up using a huge portion of a computer’s memory and processing power, which negatively impacts overall performance. For an app that is primarily meant for communication, its resource usage is surprisingly high. There’s a lot to like about Discord, but the lack of optimization and reliability is becoming increasingly frustrating.

title: Плохая работа администраторов
content:
Удалили аккаунт с причиной «мы подозреваем что вам меньше 13 лет»
Интересен тот факт что при регистрации я указывал дату Рождения и что мне 22 года. Отвязали все что можно, каналом управлять некому. Написал в поддержку отправив селфи с паспортом и с ником, их не устроило что я отправил это 2 фотками (на одной с паспортом, на другой с ником). Я телефон зубами должен держать чтобы выполнить данные условия и отправить все на 1 фотографии? Почему я после работы уставший, должен делать какие-то глупые фотки чтобы меня потом отшили? Причём это уже 3 раз удаления моего аккаунта, может создадите базу данных где это все будет числиться и фиксироваться? К самому приложению вопросов нет все сделано на высшем классе, но работа администрации портит репутацию ваших заслуг.

title: Приложение хорошее, но поддержка...
content: Начну с того, что дискорд хорошое приложение для мощных устройств. Однажды я снимал ролик и в голосовом канале со мной было 200+ человек. Я был там с телефона. IPhone XR нагревался и оооочень быстро разряжался. С маломощными компьютерами будешь так, даже если вы разговариваете вдвоём и вы хотите включить демонстрацию экрана. Скажу честно: на оценку повлияло отношение поддержки ко мне. В T&S (правила дискорда) есть очень много недочётов. Так вот когда мне было 14 лет (сейчас 15) на меня кинули жалобы с пустых аккаунтов. Сказали, что мне нет 14 лет. Я 2 месяца активно общался с ужасной поддержкой, которая посол фото с паспортом РФ и листком с моим ником написала, что мне нет 18 и меня не разблокируют. Ссылались на NSFW. А я был администратором нескольких больших серверов и покупал нитро много раз. Кстати никому не советую, потратил 100+ долларов и получил бан, который удалил мой аккаунт со всеми значками( Но за возможности приложения даю 2/5

title: Тотальное разочарование
content:
У вас бабки текут рекой за подписки, я не знаю на что они тратятся 

1. Когда пишешь длинное сообщение в личном диалоге курсор начинает «задирать» на верхнюю строчку при каждом вводе новой буквы. Проблема стара как мир.
2. Голосовые обрезаются по принципу рулетки. В моменте вам может повезти и записанная голосовуха попадёт к адресату в задуманном формате, а следующая голосовуха длинной в 30сек/минута/не дай бог 2 мин. и больше режутся нещадно до размера 5-10 сек и восстановлению не подлежат. Пожелание пользователям запоминать что они рассказывают.
3. Голосовые от собеседника в принципе могут не грузиться, клиент крашится в такие моменты и закрывается. Может потребоваться от часа для корректной загрузки.
4. Задержки периодические в приватном звонке. И этому уже ничего не поможет кроме завершения разговора в принципе и переход в другой мессенджер 
5. Сообщения отправляются долго и не доходят до отправителя.

У меня актуальный смартфон и все вышеперечисленные косяки активны когда у меня все остальные мессенджеры включая голосовую связь работают на ура. 
Удачи разработчикам.

title: текстовые каналы на серверах ужасны
content:
1) В текстовых каналах постоянной сбрасывается «последнее прочитанное сообщение», допустим, не заходил в канал целый день, там 50+ сообщений, при переходе в этот канал рандомно может спустить к самому последнему отправленному, проигнорировав то, на котором ты остановился, и сняв с него пометку о «не прочитанном», в итоге тебе нужно листать ленту вверх, и искать то самое последнее сообщение по памяти. 
2) Так же, если читать ленту сообщений в текстовом канале из 500+ не прочитанных сообщений, тебя начинает рандомно кидать то вниз, то вверх по ленте на 10-50 сообщений, если кто-то будет писать новые сообщения в этот канал, пока ты читаешь старые. 
3) Прогрузка ленты сообщений в текстовых каналах «снизу-вверх», при этом нажимая на синюю плашку «перейти к последнему прочитанному сообщению» вас будет поднимать вверх всего на 20-30 сообщений, и если их в общем будет 1000+, вам надо сидеть и тыкать 10 минут на эту кнопку, попутно подгружая всю ленту, вместо того, чтобы 
сразу перейти к последнему прочитанному в один клик.

title: Discord
content:
Discord is a social space among which you can interact as a community, as friends, or anything else alike. Discord's moderation is mediocre, with barely any attention spent on many users being reported as harassers, p***philes, and even r***sts. These kinds of users explore the foundations of Discord frequently, and often dwell in servers that advertise themselves as an "e-girl" or "dating" server. They promote this, and garner hundreds of thousands of members that often end up as victim to the ploys of these sick people. Time and time again, Discord has proven that they only prioritise a quick buck over the safety of their customers, let alone members. Their moderation is poor, servers go unnoticed, dating servers are right there on the library in trending servers, with clear intentions to promote dating, despite it violating their own TOS. It's beautiful how, despite being practically a social media app, they don't consider the safety of their users and promote this kind of behaviour, that opposes their own TOS. Zero self-respect?

Do what you want with this review, Discord. However, in the end, if you don't do anything right with your moderation and step up to do something, you all will be the center of a trending news story. Good luck. I wish a safe stay to all the users—recent or old.

title: Used to be good
content: I have been using discord since Nov 2017. There was nothing like discord back then, there were things like TeamSpeak, which weren't straight forward. I have loved using this app since then, but I have seen the gradual shift in the company's goals. The corporate greed got to them. You could see changes being made that were only made to extract more money from the users. They added paywalls for things that were free, they removed a lot of things from the Nitro basic, and moved them all to the upper tier, to the point where Nitro basic is basically useless. They also keep making changes just to make changes, with nothing actually being gained. For example, the recent overhaul of the UI. Oh I wish discord mobile app had a different UI said no one. It's soo bad to the point it feels they took a step backwards. Everything used to feel seem less, it all worked and made sense. Now I feel soo much friction while using the app. And it is not even the kind of friction where you get used to it, none of the UI element placements make sense. None of it functions smoothly. It makes me wonder, did anyone at discord even use this before approving it?

author: Sj1429

title: Screen share for PS5
content:
Discord is an amazing platform for communication, but one major limitation on PS5 really needs attention.

Right now, if you’re using Discord on PlayStation 5, there’s no proper way to stream your screen directly to a Discord voice channel. Instead, you’re forced to use PS Share, which only works with other PS5 users. This completely breaks the experience—especially if you’re in a Discord VC with friends on different platforms.

The biggest issue is that you have to leave your Discord voice chat just to share your screen through PlayStation. That defeats the whole purpose of Discord as a cross-platform communication tool. It makes streaming gameplay to friends inconvenient and honestly frustrating.

It would be a huge improvement if Discord added native screen streaming support on PS5, just like it works on PC and mobile. Being able to stay in a voice channel and stream your gameplay seamlessly would make the experience much smoother and more enjoyable.

Please consider adding this feature—it's something a lot of users would genuinely benefit from.

title: Does not understand how iOS works
content:
1. Human enables 2FA on Discord
2. Human tries to login
3. Discord App navigates to I Am Not A Robot
4. Discord navigates to ask for 2FA
5. Human opens Google Auth to get 2FA token
6. Human reads 2FA goes back to Discord
7. Discord App has gone back to pre-login screen
8. Human goes to Step 2

Human weeps

Edit: To make it clear - the problem with this app is you need to switch to Google Authenticator app during the login flow to get the 2FA token. However when you switch to Google Authenticator and then come back to this app, it resets you back to the first step of the login flow instead of staying at the 2FA prompt and you have to restart the whole thing from scratch including the CAPTCHA. The only way to login with 2FA on this app is to read the 2FA token from Google Authenticator first and then start login OR have the 2FA app on another device and read the token from there. This is the only app which I have on iOS that does this.

author: Mahirupaddhyay

title: Life changing
content:
Discord has changed my life.  Like many people it has thoroughly converted me and I suggest many other people join.  The big downside is that it’s not beginner friendly at all. You have to be very lucky to find a nice server at first or even work out where to locate servers.  Having used it for years though and being very familiar with it I think there is no better social media, no better communication tool.  I would definitely recommend it but only if you have the sort of personality which doesn’t give up, you’re the sort of person who can stand to research and find the right servers. Join hundreds before finding the right ones.  Once you get on a good server though it’s like coming home and finding a family, a community.  I think that’s what discord has more than any other social media.  A sense of community.  I would personally recommend Disboard as a way to search for servers, it’s where I advertise my server Hogwarts 2.0.  It may be less popular than Discord Me, but it is so much easier to set up, so you’ll find a lot fewer invalid links from people who haven’t configured the settings properly.  

All I would say is jump in and give it a go!  It’s daunting at first but so worth it.  I wish you luck and have fun. 

Ps.  Since this is a review of the app I should probably actually describe the experience. It is very smooth and well developed but could do with giving more pointers as to how to use it and there are lots of features you are locked out of on a phone compared to a computer.
author: elkinahole

title: Discord - pros and cons
content: Discord is an app where you can join different communities and make new friends, or keep in contact with family/ friends. You can also make your own server and give out unique rolls to different members while you can create your own emoji’s and stickers. However, the downside of discord is that you have to pay for nitro which I think is really unfair because half of the prices go up to £100 just to boost a server and it’s unfair because not everyone can afford that money. I’d recommend toning down the prices a bit. I get it, we all need to make money at some point in our life’s, but you should think about setting responsible prices for an app and make Nitro cheaper…£100 for an app is just a bit much. I don’t think I would want to pay £100 for an app when I could be using that money to pay for a roof over my head. That much money is just as much how i would need to pay bills and it’s not fair on a lot of people. Not everyone has a rich life! The app does crash now and then but they fix it almost immediately, which is a good thing. They also have support which is another good thing because if you got bullied or harassed in servers/ chats, you can report the situation to Discord. You can also block any user if they make you uncomfortable. Overall, Discord is great. It’s a very chill place when you want to chill in your free time. The only downside of the app is the prices of Nitro and the boosts. In my opinion I think that customising your profile should be for free.
author: Emily Roberts,age 20

title: The Continuation of these decisions will ruin Discord.
content:
I cannot begin to express how much I love, enjoy and appreciate discord, the app is amazing in every way, it’s useful and easy to access, a good way of being social and finding friends whether in general or on the gaming side of things, I’m in a community that I couldn’t be more thankful and grateful to be apart of. Here is the annoyance of discord, NITRO! Every business, every employee, every customer, every user understands the need for a subscription, it helps supports the business and makes it easier for everyone (in some cases) I do not kind the advertising of the subscription, what annoys me is that it limits features to the point where there’s no choice but to buy nitro, I don’t want to. The pricing is ridiculous. But I understand the point in doing it, the really frustrating part is that I can send ONE photo that’s the size of 10MB that is beyond ridiculous, there is no reason for it, I can’t send a good quality photo or video showing off my skills in the work of art unless it’s 10MB or less, by all means have a subscription, but don’t take away from the foundation that is discord. Charge people for profile customisation, boosting a server, but don’t lock key features behind a paywall, that’s just ridiculous.

Other than that, the app is flawless.

title: Hmmm
content: When the app works it’s great, you can customise your channel, add bots and do all sorts of things. Perfect for phones and tablets to be in voice communication with fellow gamers. If you keep it logged in tho there doesn’t seem to have this issue. Another issue is that if there is a minor interruption in your WiFi it doesn’t reconnect but keeps you logged in, (people can hear you but you can’t hear anyone else)... also from time to time the server goes altogether allowing nobody online at all! This doesn’t seem to be very often but I feel that the issues regarding reconnecting after micro disconnects and the issues regarding having to stay logged in due to fear of your account being compromised is something to worry about. Who knows, by installing this app I could be being listened to even if I’m not even in a voice channel?... pls fix these issues soon. I’ve been using the app for months and have seen no attempt by the developers to correct what should be very simple errors and flaws.

title: It was good, but they ruined it with the new UI
content:
Discord in general is a brilliant app, I’ve used it for six or as years now, and always loved almost everything about it, up until now I would’ve rated it as five stars. I have never had any major issues with the app until now, they have majorly changed the mobile user interface and made almost everything less accessible, as well as removing the much loved colour scheme and changing it to a generic dark blue (this can be changed to completely white, or completely black in the settings, however if you want anything else you have to pay actual money for it). Before, the layout of the app was much the same as that on the computer but optimised for use on mobile through the use of swiping left or right to access things (intuitive and easy). The layouts are now quite different, and now in order to access the same things you must go through multiple menus.

Again, this application is brilliant for a variety of reasons, but I find it difficult to still say this as confidently with these new changes, the general opinion of which from the community has been somewhat overwhelmingly negative (my opinion included). 

Thanks for reading :)

title: One glaring issue
content: Discord is a good app. It’s a great place to meet new people, join communities and generally enjoy yourself. While you’re bound to find bad apples, generally moderation is effective at dealing with them (there are several instances where I know people who have been unfairly penalised by moderation but usually appeals and customer service can sort it out, moderation could be better though). It has its issues, but it’s functional and achieves what it’s set out to do. However, there is one glaring issue which stops me from giving it more than 1 star. In a recent update, every discord server now has 4 ‘hidden’ bot accounts that do not appear in the members list. They are bots that scrape a server for all of the messages and images sent and feeds them into an AI. This is all done without user consent and this update was added silently, so many people don’t even know about this. Frankly, this type of data stealing is disgusting and it may even be breaking some data protection laws, and I cannot give more than 1 star. If you currently use discord, then find out how to protect your data from these bots, and if you don’t use discord, keep it that way.

title: New mobile app layout is awful
content:
The new layout for the mobile version of Discord is ugly, unintuitive, buggy, unnecessary and an eyesore. Now, I understand that beauty is subjective, but when the majority of people (at least that I have spoken to) dislike the appearance of the app, you're clearly doing something wrong. The old layout was fine, and worked perfectly well. 

One of the ways in which this layout is worse is that it sends message notifications to channels you're currently in, which, especially in busier chats, can obscure text from previous messages with redundant information. I hope that this is a bug that will be fixed soon, as if it is a feature it is a horrible one that actively makes user experience worse. The way that you get to the member list or pinned messages in a channel is overly complicated in comparison to the previous version, which makes the experience of using the app far more difficult. I unfortunately have no way to explain this away as a bug. Yet another way in which this app is worse is that the in-app message notifications are in an ugly grey rather than matching the colours of the theme selected. Also, I have seen the prompt asking me to select a theme twice so far, which is rather annoying. The way to get to settings is confusing also, and as someone who enjoys being able to customise her experience in apps, the extra taps are unnecessarily cumbersome. 

Personally, I'd much rather at least have an option to get the old layout back so that I can feel familiar and comfortable with this app I use to communicate with friends. The only good thing to come of this is the swipe to reply feature, and even that came at a cost: losing the easy method to access members and pinned messages. Please either completely revert back to the original layout, or at the very least add an option to get it back locally.

author: Nillymilly

title: Alright, but they make some pretty poor decisions
content:
The platform works well, rarely experiencing outages, good latency times, very consistent. The problem is that they often try to revamp things that were perfectly fine as they were, seriously harming user experience.

Take the colour update they introduced in 2021. This was rolled out with no community feedback beforehand and ended up limiting how some users could even access the platform, as many reported the colours causing unnecessary eye strain/pain, with no way to alter it until weeks later when they introduced the saturation slider in accessibility. Too little too late.

The new UI released this year (2023) for their mobile app is another instance of this. The mobile UI worked fine for most users, but in a move which I fail to see the motivation for, they revamped it, broke muscle memory, and made no attempt to ease the change. Simply why?

Still, especially for a free to use platform, Discord is really good. I’d just really like to see them look before they leap into these big changes, as it always results in backlash for them. There are too many platforms running themselves into the ground to look like they’re doing something, and maybe Discord could demonstrate that it’s okay to not make sweeping changes as long as you’re in the green that year.

title: Discord Review
content:
It’s a good, quick replacement if you want to chat with your buddies while you’re travelling or something, but having it instead of the PC version wouldn’t be advised.

- While it does notify you on your phone, it doesn’t make any kind of alert noise so I’m constantly late to reply to a lot of the messages I get @‘d in, having this feature would improve greatly for more on-the-go people who have to commute daily and etc.

- There’s quite a bit of difficulty in joining new servers through bots. This might just be due to the Iphone’s app store or whatever, or because of something the bot’s doing wrong, but I always end up getting re-routed to the app store and that interferes with the joining server process, so you can only really join new servers through being invited personally or having an actual link to the discord being dm’ed to you by someone else.

- Making servers and managing them, either as a server owner or a server administrator/moderator is very tedious compared to the PC version, It’d be nice if this was improved upon so certain phone features would be improved so it is easier to navigate the server settings and etc. For example the nickname change option is hidden under 3-4 menus and sub menus, when It could be just holding onto your status changer in the bottom left corner and then pressing change nickname through that or something.

Overall, discord is still my no.1 app for socialising online but I would recommend getting another version of discord along with it, and using this one as a temporary replacement if you want to chat to your buddies without access to a PC or one of the other platforms that you can run discord on.

title: Treats users like small children
content:
Discord is a great platform in general. It’s allowed a huge variety of wide-ranging communities to grow and flourish, in an era where other social media platforms seem to be intent on driving them away.  

But the Discord iOS app is a gimped experience that treats its users like small children who can’t make their own decisions when it comes to viewing NSFW content. Even worse, Discord pretends to give its users a choice by including a setting on their desktop app to “show NSFW on iOS”, but this setting doesn’t actually work! NSFW servers are just as blocked whether the setting is on or off.

Now, I’m sure Discord would protest: “it’s the App Store guidelines, it’s not our fault!” So why hasn’t it been a problem until now? And how do other apps with much bigger customer bases - like Twitter and Reddit - handle this issue? Far better than Discord’s developers, cowed into submission by the mighty App Store, at the expense of the communities it claims to support.

author: Debra johnes

title: Absolutely terrible, UI
content: The trajectory of Discord's mobile app suggests a concerning decline in user experience, with the current state being outright frustrating. The persisting issues in voice channels remain a thorn in the user's side, exacerbating the communication process. Camera feeds, intended to enhance interactions, sporadically malfunction, adding a layer of unpredictability to the platform. The recent UI update, while presumably aiming for improvement, has paradoxically resulted in a more convoluted and cumbersome navigation experience. Users find themselves grappling with an interface that seems to prioritize aesthetics over functionality, making routine tasks needlessly intricate. The shift has prompted some to humorously propose renaming the app "Disorganised" to reflect the chaos introduced by these changes. The collective sentiment suggests a desire for Discord to address these nuanced concerns and restore a seamless mobile experience.

author: protectmydata

title: The new UI is an accessibility nightmare.
content:
Only within the last few days as of writing this, Discord has rolled out a new UI, and it’s awful. 
I’ve been a daily Discord user for almost 4 years now, and the old UI was perfect for me! I have never had an issue with it. Neither had most users. However this new UI has been forced upon every user (whether they had auto updates on or not), with no option to revert back. 
Three things stand out:
1. The new colour options. All of them are bad. Light mode is too bright, and for many people such as those prone to migraines are unable to use it. Dark mode is too dark (as opposed to the previous grey colour) and the contrast is higher, so many people with a variety of visual problems are finding the app hard to look at or even physically painful to use. Midnight mode is just a worse dark mode. 
2. The new layout. Everything has been split into unnecessary tabs. Whilst the server tab remains mostly the same, the main search function and member list view are now compacted into one place and more awkward to access and use. DMs have changed entirely, and settings has more tabs than necessary. This is inaccessible for so many, especially those who rely on routine or have cognitive disabilities. 
3. In general, the app is now more prone to lag and slowness, both due to the new layout being unnecessarily complicated and general app performance. 
Overall, a perfectly good messaging app has been ruined in favour for a needlessly confusing UI, making it more inaccessible without fixing the already existing accessibility problems (e.g. not enough contrast/colour settings). 
Discord need to get their game on to focus on the real app problems instead of forcing users into an unwanted app design just to fit in with the competition. It’s disgraceful.

on top of profiles, i would like for usernames and server names not to be italic as some people have symbols in their user and with the italic, they do look quite silly.

title: No obvious documentation on supported video formats makes video sharing difficult.
content:
When trying to share videos, it becomes clear that many video formats don’t work in Discord’s app. For example, webms seem to play fine in Discord in the browser, even on mobile, but they won’t play in this app.

It wouldn’t be as much of an issue if Discord had a page on what video formats work on which devices, yet there is no clear information on what formats can be used. Discord has a video codecs faq page that seems to suggest that AV1 is supported, but last time I tried to upload an AV1 mp4, it didn’t work. The only way to test if a video will work seems to be to actually try posting it!

MP4s with h264 seem to be the only safe option right now, but these video files easily get too big.

Adding AV1/webm playback support to the app doesn’t seem like it should be a problem, since they seem to play just fine in mobile browsers, but the app still strangely doesn’t seem to support them. …or even list what it does support!

title: Feature Request — Clear Recent Search, Files, and Links History in Discord Ap
content:
Hi Discord Team,

I love using Discord on my iPad, but I’ve noticed that the app keeps showing recent search suggestions, recently used files, and links, which build up over time and cannot be cleared or disabled by users. This can clutter the interface and raise privacy concerns.

Could you please consider adding features that allow users to clear or disable their recent search history, recent files, and recently shared links? Having control over these histories would improve the user experience and privacy significantly.

Thanks so much for your continued work on Discord!

title: Einklappen von ausgeblendeten Nachrichten blockierter Benutzer funktioniert nicht mehr
content: Seit einiger Zeit habe ich das Problem, dass ich ausgeblendete Nachrichten von blockierten Benutzern nicht mehr einblenden kann. Es passiert einfach nichts, wenn ich die Nachrichten einblenden möchte. Ich kann dann auch keine Nachrichten mehr schreiben. Wechsel ich dann zu einem anderen Server/Channel oder zu den Direktnachrichten seh ich weiterhin den letzten Screen aus dem Channel, in dem ich Nachrichten einblenden wollte. Scrolle ich stattdessen nach oben/unten, werden keinerlei frühere oder spätere Nachrichten mehr angezeigt, selbst wenn ich direkt davor schon mal dahin gescrollt habe und Nachrichten geladen und angezeigt wurden. Dieses Verhalten tritt fast jedes Mal auf, wenn ich versuche, ausgeblendete Nachrichten anzeigen zu lassen. Ich kann dann immer nur die App beenden und neu starten und einen großen Bogen um ausgeblendete Nachrichten machen, um die App weiterhin nutzen zu können. Bitte behebt das Problem, da die App für mich so nicht mehr vernünftig nutzbar ist. Ein weiteres nerviges Problem, wenn auch nicht so gravierend: immer wieder verschwindet die Markierung für ungelesene Nachrichten am App Icon nicht, obwohl die ungelesenen Nachrichten gelesen wurden und auch entsprechend in der App nicht mehr als ungelesen angezeigt werden. Auch hier hilft nur: App beenden, Markierung ist noch da. App öffnen. App beenden. Markierung ist weg.

title: Eine geniale Idee mit einem Datenschutzproblem
content:
Ich finde die Grundidee von Discord richtig gut: Jeder kann Server erstellen, teilen und nach Belieben gestalten (mit Bots, Kanälen, Rollen etc.).
Das Finanzierungsmodell mit Discord Nitro finde ich sehr gut, Server Boosts okay, wobei das in Summe schon sehr teuer wird und, um als Server für voll genommen zu werden, leider notwendig ist.
Das Bot-Modell ist einsame Spitze, die Möglichkeit, die App nach Belieben zu Erweitern, macht sie sehr viel langlebiger und unabhängiger von den eigentlichen Entwicklern.
Ein echtes Manko ist der Datenschutz: Discord ist nicht verschlüsselt und kann absolut alles mitlesen oder -hören und versucht, möglichst viele Daten von den Nutzern zu sammeln.

Ich muss also bei einem Mal Discord benutzen gut und gerne mal 6 Mal die App neustarten. title: Bewertung von Discord
content:
Hiermit bewerte ich die App „Discord“:

Download (5/5):

Der Download läuft am Handy sowohl als auch am Laptop einwandfrei. Relativ schnell sogar. Sehr bemerkenswert!

Server erstellen (4/5):

Allgemein finde ich das man viele Möglichkeiten für seinen Server hat. Aber als Anfänger auf Discord ist es schwer, sich ohne Tutorial durchschlagen zu können. Ich würde für das Server erstellen ein Tutorial relativ gut finden! 😊

Voice Chat (4,5/5):

Folgendes: Komischerweise funktioniert am Handy der Voice Chat einwandfrei. Aber wenn ich mit meinen Freunden am PC reden will, dann hängt zunächst bei mir der Voice Chat eine Weile lange, was mich einwenig stört.

Text Chat (4,5/5)

Einwandfrei. Am Handy läuft alles blendend. Am Laptop ebenfalls, aber am Laptop werden mir nur bestimmte Emojis angezeigt. Ich weiß nicht ob es an meinem Laptop liegt, oder an Discord —� aber falls es an Discord liegt, bitte ändern!

Allgm. (9,5/10):
Eine super App mit der man viel Spaß haben kann! Dank Discord habe ich so viele neue Freunde kennengelernt, mit denen ich sogar vorhabe mich mal zu treffen! Super App! 💖

2) bei den Nachrichten die oben als Push rein kommen, ist die preview nun ausgegraut und schlecht lesbar. 
3) die DMs ploppen nicht mehr über den Severn auf, sondern nur unten im Tav gibt es klein pings zu sehen. Absolute fehlgestaltung, man sieht die DMs kaum.
4) die DMs sind nur umständlich und getrennt von den Servern und schlecht zu erreichen, die message preview im DMs tab ist störend.
5) das “runde” Design beißt sich.
6) neue Symbole sind verkindlicht und sehen viel zu verspielt aus, die alten simplen Symbole waren besser sichtbar.
7) die member Listen von Servern sind nicht wie gewohnt durch einen swipe zu sehen sondern können nur durch umständliches klicken erreicht werden. 

Alles in allem wurden viele allseits beliebte Features von discord durch neue, umständliche ersetzt und das Design verkindlicht. 
Ich hoffe, dass es wieder Rückschritte geben wird.

Musste mein Abo kündigen, weil ich Nitro sowieso geschenkt bekam, Fazit: hat überhaupt nichts gebracht, meine Freundin hat umsonst Geld ausgegeben, weil man das Geschenk sowieso nicht einlösen kann, sondern nur, wenn man ein JAHRESABO auf PC/Browser einlöst. Das ist ne bodenlose Frechheit, früher war das nie so. Ich würds ja am liebsten direkt löschen, aber dann kann ich mit vielen Leuten nicht schreiben und meine eigenen Server wären komplett weg und alles was ich da die letzten Jahre geschrieben hab, wär komplett umsonst gewesen. Meine Abzeichen waren mir immer wichtig auch das Design etc., Aber den Support intressiert es nicht die Bohne, was man für Probleme hat, am besten nicht helfen und weiter Geld einsacken. Wirklich eins der schlechtesten Unternehmen des Jahrtausends!

title: Keine Anleitung
content:
Wir finden keine Möglichkeit, Freunde einzuladen. Wir suchen einen QR-Code oder einen Link oder eine Nummer oder irgendwas, um eine Einladung zum Beispiel über Telegramm oder sonst wie zu verschicken. Wenn man eine Hilfe-Anleitung sucht, landet man auf einer Seite, die nicht angezeigt werden kann. Es kommt eine Fehlermeldung. Somit können wir diese App nicht testen und versuchen eine neutrale Wertung abzugeben. 

Familienmitglieder fragen mich, was für eine App das ist. Sie starten die App, aber dann wissen Sie immer noch nicht, was für eine App das ist. Besser wäre es, wenn es einen Startbildschirm der App gäbe, so dass Omas und Opas ungefähr wüssten, um was es da geht. So müssen die Familien Mitglieder immer erst warten, bis ich aus der Arbeit komme und frage mich dann, was das ist. So ein Blödsinn. Apps sollten selbsterklärend sein.

title: Skype 2.0
content:
Ich mag Discord, sehr sogar, aber mit jedem Update wird die App auf allen Mobilgeräten und Desktop sogar immer weniger und weniger stabil. Mittlerweile kann ich einen einfachen Anruf kaum noch halten, ohne, dass der Anruf alle 1-2 Minutes für 10-20 Sekunden abstürtzt. Mit jedem Patch kommen neue unnötige Features nach denen keiner gefragt hat und verlangsameren das Erlebnis noch mehr als es ohnehin schon geworden ist. Wenn ich Nachrichten oder Videos verschicke, sehe ich diese oft selbst nicht, obwohl sie bei allen anderen angekommen sind.

Ich hab’s satt alle paar Jahre nach einer neuen Plattform zum Labern mit Freunden suchen zu müssen und ich dachte Discord wäre da, durch diese simple Perfektion endlich Schluss damit. Ich bin echt enttäuscht wie es ausgeartet ist und werde bis es besser wird zu Telegram wechseln.

Und als dann diese Hürde überwunden war, sollte ich Captchas lösen. Nach 20 habe ich aufgehört. „Bist du ein Mensch?“.
Sorry, aber das ist völlig kaputt. Ich werde jetzt nicht mein iPad neu starten, die App neu installieren, das WLAN des Nachbarn benutzen, oder den Support kontaktieren, nur um in eine App mal kurz reinzuschauen. So schwer kann eine Anmeldung nicht sein - bei hunderten anderen Apps geht‘s ja auch ohne Probleme.

title: You had a decent thing going, and you ruined it.
content:
I’d rate 0 stars if I could, but I can’t.  Don’t use this service anymore.  Discord no longer values the safety and privacy of its users, and they definitely don’t deserve your money anymore.

This username change seriously has me considering canceling my Nitro and switching to a new application.  There was nothing, nothing at all, wrong with the current discriminator system you guys had going.  The pomelo system is a terrible system and doesn’t fit the needs of the online population on other sites, let alone on Discord, so why would you guys take a currently working system and switch to something that nobody wanted?

You’re making it easier for people to get harassed over their usernames, making it easier for stalkers to track down their victims because now there’s only one username per person, accounts will be hacked or the owners will be harassed and threatened/blackmailed into selling their accounts for profit, or worse - swatted like that poor man on Twitter who died from after he was swatted IRL, orchestrated by people who wanted his username.  A man is DEAD IRL, because someone valued a USERNAME over a human life. Congratulations, Discord, this is the possibility you’re now opening up your users to.

This update takes away any security you guys had, over a made up issue that nobody was complaining about.  You’re not helping anybody with this new system, and it’s going to cause WAY more problems in the near future than it’s going to solve.

300 million people on this platform and your solution to “there’s too many x” is to make it so there can only be ONE? Where is the logic?

title: I love discord BUT
content:
I love using discord, it is one of the only social platforms I use! But with the new update to the app, they made it so much worse. In this review I will detail what I mean specifically.

1: they moved the dm section from the top of the server list to a bar at the bottom of the screen. This makes it incongruous with the desktop version. 

1.5: More on the incongruity between the app the the desktop version. With the moving of the dms, the lack of perceived placement of the ‘who’s online list’ the app becomes harder to figure out if you mainly use desktop. When I first used the app version of discord, it was very intuitive because it was like the desktop version. Making them mismatch breeds confusion when trying to learn the app.

2: They have made it so that swiping to the left makes you enter reply on whatever message you had your finger on, instead of taking you to a list of who is online.

3: This may not be the case for everyone but I also experience noticeable stuttering whenever I try to switch between my list of servers, and the chat I’m in, or do anything really.

4: they made dark mode darker, which made the contrast between the words and the background worse, it makes my eyes hurt and borders on giving me a headache.

5: More minor dislikes. I do not like the new headphones icon, headphones like that would never sit comfortably on your head. 

5.1: I may be off my rocker for this one, but, I find that most of the new icons just look unfriendly, and harsh. 

5.2: There wasn’t a need to change the server sections icon to a group of houses, that is the section for what discord as a platform is known for, it made sense to have the logo there.

title: Disappointing Discord Update – A Struggle for Autistic Users
content: As an individual with autism, I find Discord's new UI update to be deeply challenging. The relocation of swipe features has created an unnecessary hurdle, disrupting the intuitive flow that many of us rely on for comfort and efficiency. The visual overhaul is not only jarring but fails to consider the needs of neurodivergent users who often thrive on familiarity. What's particularly disheartening is the absence of an option to revert to the old appearance. The sudden, major change feels overwhelming and unsettling, neglecting the diverse user base that Discord serves. Autistic individuals, like myself, often find solace in routine and familiarity, and this update has regrettably disrupted that equilibrium. Discord's decision to implement such a drastic change without adequate consideration for neurodivergent users reflects a lack of empathy and understanding. This update not only misses the mark on user experience but also leaves a significant portion of its community feeling disregarded and disconnected. One star for a UI update that not only misses the mark but actively infringes on the comfort and accessibility of autistic individuals.

title: Oppressive Design
content:
As of the recent update (AppleVer.209.0), Discord Mobile has been reduced to a sad, generic social media platform. 

Discord used to be simple, the Servers and Direct Messages were easy to navigate; You could look at a orderly list of your online friends and their current activity; The Profile Editor was simple but effective. 
The Old Discord Mobile was perfectly fine the way it was. 

The new Discord Mobile? 

The Discord Team has gutted the clean app design and replaced it all with an unintuitive mess of bubble buttons and cluttered “organization”. 

The current Discord Mobile is akin to a Social Media Platform, with “adjusted” categories and changed inputs, this app feels more like a mix between Instagram and Snapchat. 

Here is a breakdown of the actual problems that the new UI has:

“Swipe to Reply” causes many issues as it makes app navigation more difficult. The whole purpose of “Swipe to Reply” is to make it easier for people to use one hand while texting. There is no reason to use only one hand while on Discord. This also conflicts with the next point. 

The app is now organized into 4 categories of “Servers”, “Messages”, “Notifications”, and “You”. The old UI had servers and Messages in the same section. This was convenient as it condensed the two categories into one, and it was set up in a relatively easy to navigate manner. While it is arguably easier to navigate the app now compared to before thanks to this separation, you have to ask why they were separated. It is now easier to open the server tab on the new UI when using only one hand. Thats fine and all until you look at the server tab. It is organized in the exact same way as it used to be, servers on the left side, starting from the top of the screen down to the bottom. This is contradictory to the main argument of using the new UI, as it is equally as difficult to navigate the servers tab with one hand now as it was in the previous UI. 

There are also “features” that aren’t clear, double tapping the “You” page to quickly go to settings, but adding no other double tap features for the other tabs? 

All of these statements have been ignoring my preference for the way the app *Looks* and has focused on how it *Feels* and how it *Works*. This app Feels and Works like a mix of Instagram and Snapchat, yes, but it Looks much, much worse than both of those apps. 

The design also has flaws. Everything feels round and clunky. I want to see what my friends are up to? I have to open their DM, and click on their profile. Why am I going to their DM instead of clicking on their profile at the top of the page? Because the top of the page has both missing entries and no organization to its order. How am I supposed to find my friend’s status in the top row when it is that unreliable. 

Everything is overly large and unexplained. It made a ugly pallet change from the dark grey to a navy/dark blue, and the Midnight theme is not a good alternative. Everything is now swipe swipe swipe. This is just sad. You took a good thing and destroyed it. 

And worst of all? Discord has decided to not let users revert to the old UI. It has been stated in their update FAQ, and it is depressing that they are restricting its users like this. Especially for those on the Apple platform, not being able to re-install an older version of the app with an APK file. 

TLDR: New Discord UI bad. Old Discord UI good. Bring back Old UI. Throw out the New UI.

title: It's gotten worse
content:
Discord is a great app, I mainly don't have too many issues with it but within the last year I've noticed a lot of things that just annoy me. 1. Sitting in a call will sometimes force me out and back in within a second, causing me to have to turn speaker back on. 2. Unstable Internet Connection when coming back into the app when somebody's camera was on. 3. Camera resolution is messed up. Outside of full screen it's normal but once I try to full screen whether it's vertical or horizontal, it's zoomed in without a way to zoom out. 4. Blurred profile pictures glitching in the background of 1 on 1 calls. All of these are on the latest version of Discord on iOS at the time of this review.

New addition of complains regarding the new UI (once again on latest iOS update):

My app is incredibly broken. 1. If you leave the app and come back in, EVERY TIME you are forced to close it because it’s seemingly stuck, no buttons to push, sliding your thumb doesn’t work either. 2. Bring back the old camera system where it full screens automatically, at least in 1 on 1 calls. It’s ridiculous how I have to full screen myself to even know what’s in frame. 3. Opening discord will also sometimes leave the app blank with no UI at all anywhere except the profile section, leading me to closing the app AGAIN. 4. GIFs do not play anymore when receiving or sending, even if I click on it. 

If you’re going to make a mobile port to your app and completely “redo” it, work on the actual app itself instead of just slapping a bandaid on a sinking ship. My experience with discord has seriously declined over the past 6 months because of unfixed issues.

title: New UI is a Disaster
content:
The app used to work fine, but recently they updated the app with a new UI.
I don’t mind the new look, but with it they took several useful features away. 
The old UI used to show me how many unread messages I had in my DMs, and the accounts with messages would always be available at the top until I read them. Now, I can still see my *total* number of unread messages, but when I open the DM section it only shows me who is read and who is unread, without telling me if each person sent me one message or sent me twenty. It also no longer puts unread messages at the top. I have to scroll down and click on every blue dot I see if I want to get rid of the big red “20” next to my DMs icon.
They also removed the option to search an entire server’s messages. You can only search in each channel individually now. Why is Discord removing features? There’s no good reason for any of this.

author: Lord Varl

title: Changes for the sake of changes.
content:
I have been using Discord since 2016, in that time I have seen this app make positive changes that were loved by the userbase, and make terrible changes that causes uproar. 
The new mobile UI change is the latter. Much like Reddit did a while back when they updated their UI, they gave users the option to continue using the original UI, because they understood that removing that option meant alienating those long time users, while removing accessibility from those who seek it. 
I am not opposed to Discord updating the UI, I understand that you need to pay people’s wages, but removing the option for those who want to continue using a near 10-year old layout, is asinine, especially when leading to this point Discord made sure to emphasise both would co-exist. There is a reason the original UI barely updated, because the original designers struck gold. As someone who doesn’t care what’s happening on XYZ server, or what games/media people are listening to, having those notifications clutter the new UI as opposed to clear, easy to find and read DMs and Servers, is infuriating. 
I used to support Discord monetarily for years until recently, I stopped supporting over negative changes that made the user experience worse, so I made my wallet talk. I want to pay for Nitro, support this application that I love, but terrible decision after decision pushes that desire further away. 
Discord does not need to be the next Snapchat or Instagram, you should know your existing userbase by now. Discord is a messaging application that has helped bring people together through self-made communities, that is its identity, please listen to the userbase.

title: Do not give Discord your personal information.
content: Starting early march, Discord will automatically lock all accounts into a restricted teen mode. You will be unable to join age restricted servers, send Images that might be sensitive, and you will generally have less freedom than before. Unless you upload either a face scan or government ID that confirms your age. This should be considered a breach of privacy as the app would know who you are and/or what you look like, and dangerous as they lie about deleting your personal data once your age has been verified. They keep it. This has been shown when Discord had a massive data leak in October 2025 which included almost 2 terabytes of user data, including face scans and government IDs. In general, Discord is not known for having great security, as hacks and leaks are common. Discord either needs to push back on this update and come up with a better way to keep children safe, or provide a way to ensure users that their sensitive data is not kept like promised. In the meantime, please do not give Discord your personal data as they cannot be trusted with it, and do not purchase anything from their store or subscribe to nitro. Make them aware that a large portion of their user base is not okay with this, because I sure am not right now.

author: Jojofoulk

title: UI change has brought this app from 4 stars to 1
content:
The new UI is absolutely atrocious. Numerous users have been complaining about accessibility issues (such as the decision to alter the dark mode to make it *less* accessible to users with astigmatism), poor design, moving essential app features previously accessible through a single swipe or tap to behind multiple swipes, taps and button presses seemingly moved to completely obscure locations. Additionally, the new UI features a number of (potentially dangerous) bugs, ranging from infinite loading screens to crashing when certain inputs are made (amusingly, the ‘feedback’ button has caused numerous users’ apps to crash when pressed) to sending DMs to the wrong person, or even to a server. 

While the ‘new’ UI has been available for a number of months, discord has always included the option to instead use the old one for users who prefer it. Removing that option was an unfortunate sign in the decline in quality of the developers’ responses to user feedback, and is a major blight on what has otherwise been an amazing app up until this point.

title: It's fine
content:
I've been using discord for a few years now, but all the recent changes have been generally for the worse. 
The major user-interface change for the phone app version is one of my major gripes, it feels like a copy-paste from messenger but somehow even worse. The older layout that's still on other versions of the platform was a bit confusing to me as a new user but is way more fluid to use than typical messaging app layouts.
Additionally, discord recently lowered the free upload limit to just 10MB, as if most modern files, including a simple screenshot, aren't around 15MB minimum. It feels as if the app is forcing users to pay for nitro, the subscription version of discord, just to use basic features like image/ video share. It really should just compress files instead of demanding you buy nitro.
There's also many persisting bugs like notifications not clearing properly, and sending videos from inside discord (at least on the phone app) occasionally turns them into a useless file link that you can't open by phone. The search-within-chat feature is unusable, and rarely gives you all the messages that actually contain what you're looking for. This also used to function a lot better before the big UI overhaul.

author: The Cool and Extreme Gamer

title: When Discord Support Doesn’t Help
content:
When I first got Discord, I genuinely loved it. It felt like an amazing place to connect with friends, join communities, and have fun conversations. Everything about it seemed easy, welcoming, and enjoyable, and I spent a lot of time on the platform because of how much I liked it.

But over time, my experience has completely changed. Now, Discord feels frustrating and disappointing. The biggest issue was when my account got hacked, which was honestly stressful and upsetting. I lost access and felt like my privacy and security had been completely violated.

What made things worse was how the situation was handled when I tried to get help. I reached out to moderators hoping for support or at least some guidance, but instead of actually helping me resolve the issue, they just told me to submit a request. That process feels incredibly unhelpful and impersonal. It doesn’t give any immediate support, and it feels like your problem just gets pushed into a queue where nothing actually happens for a long time—if anything happens at all.

From my experience, making a request feels like shouting into the void. There’s no real reassurance, no clear timeline, and no guarantee that your issue will even be properly looked at. When you’re dealing with something serious like a hacked account, being told to just “make a request” feels dismissive and frustrating, especially when you’re already stressed and need urgent help.

Overall, the whole experience left me feeling let down. A platform I used to enjoy and trust now feels unreliable, especially when it comes to handling serious issues like account security and user support.

If you have cash, it is worth throwing some dollars at the developers to say thank you.

For community, the ease at which members can freely create their own servers results in community splintering.  The benefit of community and meeting like minded individuals across a large range of games is hindered.  

I would love to see better community tools similar to a town square with shops all around.  Meet new people before heading of to play.

The developers are responsive with new features regularly coming online.

In my opinion, this is the best communication tool at this time.  I look forward to watching how this develops in the future.

Thanks developers.

Highly recommended.

title: New UI :(
content:
The new UI places private messages in the bottom menu on the screen instead of above servers — this majorly lowers visibility and leads to missing notifications. I didn’t realise I had messages for a while because of this :(

It has also changed to swipe-to-reply to messages in chats, which has replaced the prior slide ability to view online server members. This option is now hidden behind two steps, and doesn’t even grey-out offline members. 

The search function has also changed now: when it used to be a server-wide search is now on a single channel basis, meaning if you are looking for something in particular but don’t know where it is, it is now an entire ordeal to find

Overall, these new features drastically lower the usability of the app and are inefficient; especially when long-time users have everything down by muscle memory. 

(To note: I also got warning of this UI update from a friend and turned off auto app updates in preparation only to find the change happened anyway. Not happy)

title: where’d my profile customisation go?
content:
i’d say discord is a nice app, most of the time. however the more you try to change the layout, design and features the more confusing the application gets.

as a user who has spent a decent 7 months with discord, it’s safe to say that i’ve seen many ups and downs in this social media platform. the one thing that irritates me the most is how more and more special features are being locked behind a gate that we all know as discord nitro. profile banner, longer messages and animated stickers are just some of the features that can be accessible once you hit the pay button. to some people this may seem like a very reasonable advertising strategy for nitro, but to myself at least, it gets too in your face. this is merely a friendly social media platform (when pedos, trolls and racists are taken out of course) which can either be an everyday app or just an occasional socialising platform. lots of people download discord just for the sake of talking to co-workers and friends, not everyone would use it for long term/times. shoving a big ‘make discord yours’ poster with, even worse, bright and appealing colours firstly does not make sense in terms of wording, and secondly is not fair for those who consider discord an ‘occasional’ app, because in reality, it’s just another social media platform just like reddit, Twitter and Facebook (but with a much less mature user audience) and shoving an indirect advertisement for so-called discord power juice whenever innocent users try to experiment is not very fair. 

i would also like to mention the profile customisation which has recently expanded its user ‘testers’. since one of my friends was allowed access to these features, i realised I could not change my about me, or my profile banner. the option is no longer there. i would like to have them back again, for my about me is not updated.

i’d greatly appreciate it if you read this entire review. i’m kind of known for that, hah. thank you, reply is optional.

title: Looks vs Functionality
content:
Yes things could be worse, but I’ll reserve 1 star for when that happens. 

Looks wise, yes finally a dark mode, that is dark. 

However functionality, it is a huge step backwards. When you are an staff in a large server, search and pings are key. 
Search functionality is not functional. You used to be able to search a User ID and it brings back all pings from all channels or do the old “From: <user id>” in the search and it bought back all messages from that user in all channels . Now you have to hit hidden menus, be in the channel you want to search, it’s basically made modding from mobile difficult and almost impossible. 

Layouts it confuses members because hide channels is a default setting. 
Server staff get that question all the time “where are all the channels” 

Feels like all you needed to do was enable an oled design and everyone would have been happy as Larry. Hopefully you can roll back some of the functionality to make it easier on everyone

author: irisltx

title: Always a trade off
content:
Jitsi is pretty good for video chats for up to about 10 people. 

It is very easy, does not require an account and is both free and does not impose a time limit. 

The cost for this is poorer performance than a paid zoom account. We tried both, one after the other with 6 to 10 people and zoom picture was very much more stable. 

However a large group of us are using jitsi 3 times a day for an organisation that spans the world. We have a unique meeting name that allows anyone to start a meeting at any time and any body else to join in. There’s no specific host so the meeting continues even when the first person leaves. 

For some unexplained reason, it usually works better on my phone than my laptop, even though both use the same wifi network. 

If you are happy to have casual meetings and accept that performance may drop off occasionally it is a pretty good solution.

title: Poor UX
content:
First time ever leaving a review for an app, but the redesign is so egregious that it warranted it. This app is a prime example of how not to do your UI & UX. There is a substantial reduction in the user experience, such as: 

- The settings menu is hidden away under two separate submenus
- A superfluous notifications tab takes up prime real estate
- You have to select the servers menu to get… another server menu, where you can actually then select a server (for real this time)
- Layout is drastically different to the desktop app, instead of being familiar due to how similar they were
- The first element you encounter in the messages section has nothing to do with messages at all, instead giving you some kind of activity tray that provides nothing of value

Other developers, please learn from Discord’s mistakes here.

title: Awful new UI
content: I have used Discord for over 5 years and the UI has been some of the most intuitive of any chat app. In a single update they threw all of this away, leaving us with a clunky interface that is hard to navigate and slower than the original. You can no longer swipe between panels, and instead must use the navigation buttons at the bottom of your screen (which feel clunky and have unsatisfying animations). Instead of having server and DM pings all in one place along the sidebar, where you can instantly see where all notifications are coming from, notifications are hidden in a separate page that groups them all together, making it useless for someone in many different servers, who only wants to address a few different pings. Somehow discord has made their app look a lot like Guilded, their competitor with an inferior interface.

title: Unsafe and outclassed in VC by Teamspeak, useful for private chats.
content:
If you are going to be chatting for a majority of your time on Discord through voice calls, just rent a TS server. It’s simple, accessible and high quality compared to Discord’s practically authoritarian rules on bandwidth.

Use this app for communities and group chats exclusively; there’s no other multi media private chat forum on the internet that’s recognised like Discord.

The privacy on Discord is a burden and a pro, conversations never being tracked with data and a guarantee of safe person to person communication. On the other hand, Discord’s privacy makes it a lot easier for predators to take advantage of others; something not rare to the landscapes of Discord life.

Discord replaced Skype. It was a big moment - the client was clean, had basic but stable features and it quickly became a natural thing to have as a gamer.

It’ll go full circle. Discord originally replaced Skype, but Discord in its current state is just waiting to be replaced by something better.
